title.en: Volume 96 Biographies 21: Fang Xuanling, younger brothers Du Ruhui and Du Chuke, Uncle: Yan, Fifth Generation Descendent: Du Yuanying, Sixth Generation Descendent: Shen Quan, Seventh Generation Descendent: Rang Neng
title.raw: 卷九十六 列傳第二十一 房玄齡 杜如晦弟:楚客 叔父:淹 五世孫:元穎 六世孫:審權 七世孫:讓能 Volume 96 Biographies 21: Fang Xuanling, younger brothers Du Ruhui and Du Chuke, Uncle: Yan, Fifth Generation Descendent: Du Yuanying, Sixth Generation Descendent: Shen Quan, Seventh Generation Descendent: Rang Neng

sentences.zh: 房玄齡子:遺愛 杜如晦弟:楚客 叔父:淹 五世孫:元穎 六世孫:審權 七世孫:讓能

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling's son: Yiai. Du Ruhui's younger brother: Chuke. Paternal uncle: Yan. Fifth-generation descendant: Yuanying. Sixth-generation descendant: Shenquan. Seventh-generation descendant: Rangneng.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling's son, Yiai; Du Ruhui's younger brother, Chuke; their paternal uncle, Yan; fifth-generation descendant, Yuanying; sixth-generation descendant, Shenquan; seventh-generation descendant, Rangneng.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling

sentences.zh: 房玄齡，字喬，齊州臨淄人。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling, courtesy name Qiao, was a native of Linzi in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling, styled Qiao, came from Linzi in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 父彥謙，仕隋，曆司隸刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yanzhi served the Sui and successively held the post of Cishi of the Directorate of Convicts.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanzhi served under the Sui and rose to serve as inspector of the Directorate of Convicts.

sentences.zh: 玄齡幼警敏，貫綜墳籍，善屬文，書兼草隸。

translations.literal: From childhood Xuanling was quick-witted and perceptive; he mastered the classics; he was skilled at literary composition, and wrote in both cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy, Xuanling was exceptionally bright. He mastered the classical canon, wrote with ease, and was accomplished in both cursive and clerical calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，天下混壹，皆謂隋祚方永，玄齡密白父曰：「上無功德，徒以周近親，妄誅殺，攘神器有之，不為子孫立長久計，淆置嫡庶，競侈僭，相傾鬩，終當內相誅夷。

translations.literal: During the Kaihuang era, when the realm had been unified, all believed the Sui mandate would endure. Xuanling secretly told his father: "The emperor has no merit—he simply seized the imperial regalia as a close kinsman of Zhou. He kills wantonly, yet does not plan for the long-term welfare of his descendants, confuses legitimate and illegitimate succession, vies in extravagance and overstepping of rank, and contends in mutual destruction; in the end they will certainly slaughter one another within the family.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang reign, when the empire had been reunified, everyone assumed the Sui dynasty would last forever. Xuanling quietly told his father, "The throne has no true merit behind it. The emperor merely seized the Mandate because he was Zhou's nearest kin. He kills at whim, makes no lasting provision for his heirs, muddles the line between legitimate and illegitimate sons, and encourages rivalry in luxury and presumption until the court turns on itself. In the end the dynasty will devour its own."

sentences.zh: 視今雖平，其亡，跬可須也。

translations.literal: Though the world now appears peaceful, its fall can be awaited in but a short step.
translations.idiomatic: The realm may look settled now, but its collapse is only a step away.

sentences.zh: 」彥謙驚曰：無妄言！

translations.literal: " Yanzhi was alarmed and said: "Speak no rash words!
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi was startled. "Do not speak such reckless words!"

sentences.zh: 」年十八，舉進士。

translations.literal: " At age eighteen, he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 授羽騎尉，校仇秘書省。

translations.literal: He was appointed Yuji Wei and assigned to proofreading at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a captain of the Feathered Cavalry and set to collating texts in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎高孝基名知人，謂裴矩曰：「僕觀人多矣，未有如此郎者，當為國器，但恨不見其聳壑昂霄雲。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Gao Xiaoji was famed for recognizing talent. He said to Pei Ju: "I have observed many men, but never one like this young gentleman. He will be a pillar of the state—only I regret that I shall not live to see him soaring over ravines and ascending to the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xiaoji, vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, was renowned for judging men. He told Pei Ju, "I have seen countless people, but never anyone like this young man. He will be a pillar of the state. I only regret that I shall not live to see him rise like a dragon above the gorges and into the sky."

sentences.zh: 」補隰城尉。

translations.literal: " He was appointed assistant magistrate of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed assistant magistrate of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒反，坐累，徙上郡。

translations.literal: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled, he was implicated and exiled to Shang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Liang of Han rebelled, Xuanling was implicated and banished to Shang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 顧中原方亂，慨然有憂天下志。

translations.literal: Seeing that the Central Plains were in turmoil, he was moved with concern for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing chaos spread across the Central Plains, he was filled with concern for the fate of the empire.

sentences.zh: 會父疾，綿十旬，不解衣；

translations.literal: When his father fell ill, for one hundred days he did not remove his clothes;
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell ill, he tended him for a hundred days without changing his clothes.

sentences.zh: 及喪，勺飲不入口五日。

translations.literal: when his father died, for five days he took not even a spoonful of drink.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death, he took no food or drink for five days.

sentences.zh: 太宗以燉煌公徇渭北，杖策上謁軍門，一見如舊，署渭北道行軍記室參軍。

translations.literal: When the Taizong, as Duke of Dunhuang, marched north of the Wei River, Xuanling walked with a staff to the army gate to pay his respects. At first sight they were as old friends, and he was appointed Army Aide-de-Camp for the Weibei Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Taizong, then Duke of Dunhuang, campaigned north of the Wei, Xuanling came on foot with a staff to present himself at the camp gate. They met as though they had known each other for years, and he was appointed recorder for the Weibei campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 公為秦王，即授府記室，封臨淄侯。

translations.literal: When the Duke became Prince of Qin, Xuanling was immediately appointed Prince's Secretary and enfeoffed as Marquis of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: Once the duke became Prince of Qin, Xuanling was made secretary of the princely household and enfeoffed as Marquis of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 征伐未嘗不從，眾爭取怪珍，玄齡獨收人物致幕府，與諸將密相申結，人人願盡死力。

translations.literal: He never failed to accompany the prince on campaigns. While others competed to seize rare treasures, Xuanling alone gathered men of talent for the prince's staff, secretly forming close bonds with the generals, so that each wished to give his utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He never missed a campaign. While others scrambled for curios and booty, Xuanling alone recruited men of ability for the prince's staff, quietly winning over the commanders until each was ready to die for the cause.

sentences.zh: 王嘗曰：「漢光武得鄧禹，門人益親。

translations.literal: The prince once said: "When Emperor Guangwu of Han obtained Deng Yu, his disciples grew ever closer.
translations.idiomatic: The prince once said, "When Emperor Guangwu of Han gained Deng Yu, his followers drew closer to one another than ever.

sentences.zh: 今我有玄齡，猶禹也。

translations.literal: Now that I have Xuanling, he is like Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have Xuanling, he is my Deng Yu."

sentences.zh: 」居府出入十年，軍符府檄，或駐馬即辦，文約理盡，初不著稿。

translations.literal: For ten years he served in and out of the prince's headquarters. Military orders and headquarters documents—sometimes he would finish them even while still mounted on horseback; the writing was concise yet fully reasoned, and he never needed a draft.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years he moved in and out of the prince's headquarters. Orders and dispatches—sometimes drafted on horseback—were always terse, complete, and never required a second draft.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「若人機識，是宜委任。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "Such a man of insight and judgment ought to be entrusted with responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "A man of such insight deserves real trust.

sentences.zh: 每為吾兒陳事，千里外猶對面語。」

translations.literal: Whenever he reports affairs for my son, it is as though speaking face to face across a thousand li."
translations.idiomatic: When he explains matters for my son, it is as if they were talking face to face though a thousand li apart."

sentences.zh: 隱太子與王有隙，王召玄齡與計，對曰：「國難世有，惟聖人克之。

translations.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince had enmity with the Prince of Qin. The prince summoned Xuanling to consult, and he replied: "National crises occur in every age; only a sage can overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Crown Prince and the Prince of Qin were at odds. When the prince summoned Xuanling for counsel, he answered, "Every age knows national crisis; only a sage can overcome it.

sentences.zh: 大王功蓋天下，非特人謀，神且相之。

translations.literal: Your Highness's achievements cover the world—not by human planning alone, but the spirits also assist."
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness's merit fills the world. That is not human scheming alone—the spirits themselves are on your side."

sentences.zh: 」乃引杜如晦協判大計。

translations.literal: He then brought in Du Ruhui to jointly plan the great design.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought in Du Ruhui to help shape the decisive plan.

sentences.zh: 累進陝東道大行台考功郎中、文學館學士。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Langzhong of Personnel Evaluation in the Grand Commissionerate of the Shandong Circuit and Academician of the Literature Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to director of merit evaluation in the Shandong Grand Commissionerate and to academician of the Literature Hall.

sentences.zh: 故太子忌二人者，奇譖於帝，皆斥逐還第。

translations.literal: The former crown prince envied these two men and lodged strange slanders against them with the emperor; both were dismissed and sent back to their residences.
translations.idiomatic: The former crown prince resented the two men and wove odd accusations against them before the emperor. Both were expelled and sent home.

sentences.zh: 太子將有變，王召二人以方士服入，夜計事。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was about to make a move, the prince summoned the two men, who entered disguised as Taoist practitioners, to plan affairs by night.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was preparing a coup, the prince called the two men in disguised as Taoist adepts and plotted with them through the night.

sentences.zh: 事平，王為皇太子，擢右庶子。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled and the prince became crown prince, Xuanling was promoted to Right Vice Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Once the crisis was resolved and the prince became heir apparent, Xuanling was promoted to right vice tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子即位，為中書令。

translations.literal: When the crown prince succeeded to the throne, he became Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince ascended the throne, Xuanling became director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 第功班賞，與如晦、長孫無忌、尉遲敬德、侯君集功第一，進爵邗國公，食邑千三百戶，餘皆次敘封拜。

translations.literal: When merit was ranked and rewards distributed, together with Ruhui, Zhangsun Wuji, Yuchi Jingde, and Hou Junji he ranked first in achievement. He was advanced to Duke of Han State with a fief of 1,300 households; the rest were enfeoffed and promoted in descending order.
translations.idiomatic: When achievements were ranked and rewards granted, he stood first with Ruhui, Zhangsun Wuji, Yuchi Jingde, and Hou Junji. He was raised to Duke of Han with a fief of 1,300 households; the others received titles and offices in descending order.

sentences.zh: 帝顧群臣曰：「朕論公等功，定封邑，恐不能盡，當無有諱，各為朕言之。

translations.literal: The emperor turned to the assembled ministers and said: "In judging your merits and determining fiefdoms, I fear I cannot do full justice. You should have no reservations—each of you speak on my behalf."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked at the assembled ministers and said, "In weighing your service and fixing your fiefs, I fear I may fall short. Do not hold back—each of you speak for yourselves."

sentences.zh: 」淮安王神通曰：「義師起，臣兵最先至，今玄齡等以刀筆吏居第一，臣所未喻。

translations.literal: Prince Huai'an Li Shentong said: "When the righteous army rose up, my troops were the first to arrive. Yet now Xuanling and the others, mere scribes, rank first—I cannot understand this."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai'an, Li Shentong, said, "When the founding army first marched, my troops were the first to arrive. Yet now Xuanling and the rest—mere men of the brush—rank first. I do not understand it."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「叔父兵誠先至，然未嘗躬行陣勞，故建德之南，軍敗不振，討黑闥反動，望風輒奔。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Uncle, your troops did indeed arrive first, yet you never personally bore the toil of battle. Thus south of Jian De your army was defeated and failed to recover; when suppressing Hei Da's rebellion you fled at the mere sight of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Uncle, your troops did arrive first, but you never shared the hardship of the front lines. That is why, south of Dou Jiande, your army broke and could not rally, and why, when Liu Heida rebelled, you fled at the first sign of trouble.

sentences.zh: 今玄齡等有決勝帷幄、定社稷功，此蕭何所以先諸將也。

translations.literal: Now Xuanling and the others have the achievement of determining victory within the command tent and stabilizing the realm—this is why Xiao He ranked ahead of the generals."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling and the others won the war in the command tent and secured the realm. That is why Xiao He stood above the generals."

sentences.zh: 叔父以親，宜無愛者，顧不可緣私與功臣競先後爾。

translations.literal: As an uncle by blood, you ought to be without reservation—but one cannot on account of private ties compete with meritorious ministers for precedence."
translations.idiomatic: As my uncle by blood, you deserve every consideration—but kinship cannot be used to outrank men who earned their place by merit."

sentences.zh: 」初，將軍丘師利等皆怙跋攘袂，或指畫自陳說，見神通愧屈，乃曰：「陛下至不私其親，吾屬可妄訴邪！」

translations.literal: Initially, the generals Qiu Shili and others all strutted about and rolled up their sleeves, some gesturing as they stated their own cases. When they saw Shentong humiliated and abashed, they said: "Your Majesty is supremely impartial even toward his kin—how can we make reckless complaints!"
translations.idiomatic: At first the generals Qiu Shili and the rest swaggered forward, sleeves rolled up, some pointing and arguing their own cases. When they saw Shentong humbled and silenced, they said, "Your Majesty will not even favor his own kin—what grounds have we to complain?"

sentences.zh: 進尚書左僕射，監修國史，更封魏。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, overseer of the compilation of the national history, and his fief was changed to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, placed in charge of compiling the national history, and his fief was changed to Wei.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公為僕射，當助朕廣耳目，訪賢材。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "As Vice Director, you ought to help me broaden my ears and eyes and seek out talented men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "As vice director, you should help me widen my reach and find worthy men.

sentences.zh: 此聞閱牒訟日數百，豈暇求人哉？

translations.literal: Yet I hear you review several hundred petitions and lawsuits daily—where is the leisure to seek men?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hear you go through hundreds of petitions and lawsuits every day. When do you have time to search for talent?"

sentences.zh: 」乃敕細務屬左右丞，大事關僕射。

translations.literal: Thereupon he decreed that minor matters should belong to the Left and Right Assistant Directors, while major affairs would concern the Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered minor business assigned to the left and right assistant directors, while major affairs remained with the vice director.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問：「創業、守文孰難？

translations.literal: The emperor once asked: "Which is harder—founding the realm or preserving it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked, "Which is harder: founding a dynasty or preserving one?"

sentences.zh: 」玄齡曰：「方時草昧，群雄競逐，攻破乃降，戰勝乃克，創業則難。

translations.literal: Xuanling said: "At that time the age was still primitive, with rival heroes competing in pursuit; cities were taken only after being broken, enemies conquered only after being defeated in battle—founding was the harder."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling answered, "In those days the world was still raw and every warlord was fighting for supremacy. Cities fell only after siege, enemies yielded only after defeat. Founding the dynasty was the harder task."

sentences.zh: 」魏徵曰：「王者之興，必乘衰亂，覆昏暴，殆天授人與者。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said: "The rise of a true king must ride upon decline and disorder, overthrowing darkness and tyranny—it is nearly heaven conferring power upon the people's choice.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said, "The rise of a true king rides on decay and chaos, overthrowing a dark and brutal order. That is almost heaven handing the Mandate to the one the people will accept.

sentences.zh: 既得天下，則安於驕逸。

translations.literal: Once the realm is obtained, one settles into pride and idleness.
translations.idiomatic: Once the realm is won, a ruler settles into pride and ease.

sentences.zh: 人欲靜，徭役毒之；

translations.literal: When people desire rest, corvée labor poisons them;
translations.idiomatic: When the people long for peace, forced labor torments them.

sentences.zh: 世方敝，裒刻窮之。

translations.literal: when the age is already exhausted, extortion presses them to destitution.
translations.idiomatic: When the age is already worn thin, harsh exactions drive them to ruin.

sentences.zh: 國繇此衰，則守文為難。

translations.literal: When the state declines for this reason, preserving the realm becomes the harder task."
translations.idiomatic: When the state falters for these reasons, preserving it becomes the harder task."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「玄齡從我定天下，冒百死，遇一生，見創業之難。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Xuanling followed me in settling the realm, risking death a hundred times and meeting survival but once—he knows the hardship of founding.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Xuanling followed me through the conquest, facing death a hundred times and life only once. He knows how hard founding was.

sentences.zh: 徵與我安天下，畏富貴則驕，驕則怠，怠則亡，見守文之不為易。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng helped me pacify the realm; he sees that fearing wealth and honor leads to pride, pride leads to negligence, and negligence leads to ruin—he knows that preserving the realm is no easy matter.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng helped me settle the realm. He sees that wealth and rank breed arrogance, arrogance breeds slackness, and slackness breeds ruin. He knows preservation is not easy.

sentences.zh: 然創業之不易，既往矣；

translations.literal: Yet the difficulty of founding is already past;
translations.idiomatic: The hardship of founding is behind us.

sentences.zh: 守文之難，方與公等慎之。」

translations.literal: the difficulty of preservation—this is what I now ask you all to heed carefully."
translations.idiomatic: The hardship of preservation is what I now ask all of you to take to heart."

sentences.zh: 會詔大臣世襲，授宋州刺史，徙國梁，而群臣讓世襲事，故罷刺史，遂為梁國公。

translations.literal: When an edict was issued for hereditary succession among great ministers, he was appointed Prefect of Songzhou and his fief state was moved to Liang. But because the ministers yielded on the matter of hereditary succession, the prefectural post was abolished, and he became Duke of Liang State.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict granted hereditary succession to great ministers, he was made prefect of Songzhou and his fief was moved to Liang. Because the ministers declined hereditary office, the prefecture was withdrawn and he became Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，加太子少師。

translations.literal: Before long, he was additionally appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he was also made junior tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 始詣東宮，皇太子欲拜之，玄齡讓不敢謁，乃止。

translations.literal: When he first went to the Eastern Palace, the crown prince wished to bow to him. Xuanling declined and did not dare to receive the visit, and so it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On his first visit to the Eastern Palace, the crown prince wanted to bow to him. Xuanling refused, saying he dared not accept such honor, and the ceremony was dropped.

sentences.zh: 居宰相積十五年，女為王妃，男尚主，自以權寵隆極，累表辭位，詔不聽。

translations.literal: Having served as chief minister for fifteen years, with his daughter married to a prince and his son married to an imperial princess, he considered his power and favor supreme. He repeatedly memorialized to resign his office, but the edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: After fifteen years as chief minister, with a daughter married to a prince and a son married to an imperial princess, he felt his power and favor had reached their height. He memorialized again and again to resign, but the throne would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 頃之，進司空，仍總朝政。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, he was promoted to Minister of Works, yet still directed court affairs overall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to minister of works, yet still oversaw the government as before.

sentences.zh: 玄齡固辭，帝遣使謂曰：「讓，誠美德也。

translations.literal: Xuanling firmly declined. The emperor sent a messenger saying: "Yielding is indeed a fine virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling pressed his refusal. The emperor sent word: "Modesty is a fine virtue.

sentences.zh: 然國家相眷賴久，一日去良弼，如亡左右手。

translations.literal: Yet the state has long relied upon you as chief minister; to lose a fine pillar in one day is like losing both left and right hands.
translations.idiomatic: But the state has long depended on you as chief minister. To lose a good minister in a day is like losing both hands.

sentences.zh: 顧公筋力未衰，毋多讓！

translations.literal: Considering that your strength is not yet faded, do not yield overmuch!"
translations.idiomatic: Your strength is not yet spent—do not decline so often!"

sentences.zh: 」晉王為皇太子，改太子太傅，知門下省事。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jin became crown prince, Xuanling was changed to Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince and given charge of Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin became crown prince, Xuanling was made grand tutor to the heir and put in charge of Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 以母喪，賜塋昭陵園。

translations.literal: On account of his mother's mourning, he was granted a burial plot in the Zhaoling imperial park.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his mother, he was granted a burial plot in the Zhaoling park.

sentences.zh: 起復其官。

translations.literal: He was recalled to office before the mourning period ended.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to office before the mourning period had ended.

sentences.zh: 會伐遼，留守京師。

translations.literal: When a campaign against Liao was underway, he remained to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against Liaodong began, he remained behind to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「公當蕭何之任，朕無西顧憂矣。

translations.literal: An edict said: "You undertake the role of Xiao He—I need no longer worry about affairs behind me.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read, "You fill the role of Xiao He. I need no longer look back with worry.

sentences.zh: 」凡糧械飛輸，軍伍行留，悉裁總之。

translations.literal: All grain, weapons, transport by relay, and the movement and encampment of armies he decided and oversaw entirely."
translations.idiomatic: All grain, arms, transport, and the movement and disposition of the armies were entirely under his command."

sentences.zh: 玄齡數上書勸帝，願毋輕敵，久事外夷。

translations.literal: Xuanling repeatedly memorialized advising the emperor, hoping he would not despise the enemy and would not prolong campaigns against foreign peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling wrote again and again urging the emperor not to underestimate the enemy and not to prolong war against foreign states.

sentences.zh: 固辭太子太傅，見聽。

translations.literal: He firmly declined the post of Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, and his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the post of grand tutor to the crown prince, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 晚節多病，時帝幸玉華宮，詔玄齡居守，聽臥治事。

translations.literal: In his late years he was often ill. When the emperor was visiting Yuhua Palace, he ordered Xuanling to remain on guard and permitted him to govern affairs while lying down.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he was often ill. When the emperor went to Yuhua Palace, he ordered Xuanling to remain in the capital and allowed him to conduct business from his bed.

sentences.zh: 稍棘，召許肩輿入殿，帝視流涕，玄齡亦感咽不自勝。

translations.literal: When his condition worsened, he was summoned and permitted to enter the palace carried on a shoulder litter. The emperor looked upon him with tears streaming; Xuanling also choked with emotion beyond bearing.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew severe, he was summoned and allowed to enter the palace in a sedan chair. The emperor wept at the sight of him; Xuanling, too, was overcome and could not speak.

sentences.zh: 命尚醫臨候，尚食供膳，日奏起居狀。

translations.literal: He ordered court physicians to attend him in person and the Imperial Catering Office to provide meals; daily reports on his condition were submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered court physicians to attend him and the imperial kitchen to send meals, with daily reports on his condition.

sentences.zh: 少損，即喜見於色。

translations.literal: At the slightest improvement, the emperor's joy showed in his face.
translations.idiomatic: At the slightest sign of improvement, joy showed plainly on the emperor's face.

sentences.zh: 玄齡顧諸子曰：「今天下事無不得，惟討高麗未止，上含怒意決，群臣莫敢諫，吾而不言，抱愧沒地矣！

translations.literal: Xuanling turned to his sons and said: "Today there is nothing in the realm that has not been accomplished—only the campaign against Goguryeo has not ceased. The emperor harbors wrath and his resolve is fixed; none of the ministers dares remonstrate. If I do not speak, I shall carry shame into the grave!
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling turned to his sons and said, "Nothing under heaven remains undone except the war against Goguryeo. The emperor is set in angry resolve, and no minister dares speak against it. If I stay silent, I shall die ashamed."

sentences.zh: 」遂上疏曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 上古所不臣者，陛下皆臣之；

translations.literal: Those whom antiquity did not subdue as vassals, Your Majesty has all made vassals;
translations.idiomatic: Peoples whom antiquity never made submit, Your Majesty has made submit.

sentences.zh: 所不制者，陛下皆制之矣，為中國患，無如突厥，而大小可汗相次束手，弛辮握刀，分典禁衛。

translations.literal: those whom antiquity did not control, Your Majesty has all brought under control. As a scourge to China, none compared to the Turks—yet the great and lesser khans have in succession surrendered, let down their braids and taken up swords, and been assigned to command the imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: Peoples whom antiquity never controlled, Your Majesty has brought under control. Of all the threats to China, none matched the Turks—yet the great and lesser khans have surrendered one after another, cut their braids, taken up swords, and now serve in the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 延陀、鐵勒，披置州縣；

translations.literal: The Xueyantuo and Tiele were distributed and placed in prefectures and counties;
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo and Tiele were settled across prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 高昌、吐渾，偏師掃除。

translations.literal: Gaochang and Tuyuhun were swept away by detached columns.
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang and Tuyuhun were cleared by detached columns.

sentences.zh: 惟高麗歷代逋命，莫克窮討。

translations.literal: Only Goguryeo, defying imperial command through successive dynasties, could not be thoroughly pursued to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Only Goguryeo, defying the throne dynasty after dynasty, could never be fully brought to bay.

sentences.zh: 陛下責其弑逆，身自將六軍，徑荒裔，不旬日拔遼東，虜獲數十萬，殘眾、孽君縮氣不敢息，可謂功倍前世矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, holding them accountable for regicide and treason, personally led the six armies across the wild frontier regions. In less than ten days Liaodong was taken; several hundred thousand captives were seized; the remnants and the rebel ruler drew in their breath and dared not exhale—it can be said your achievement doubled that of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, charging them with regicide and treason, personally led the six armies deep into the frontier. In less than ten days Liaodong fell; hundreds of thousands were taken captive; the survivors and the rebel king held their breath in terror. Your achievement already doubles that of any earlier reign.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「知進退存亡不失其正者，其惟聖人乎！

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "He who knows advance and retreat, survival and perdition, and does not lose the proper course—is this not the sage!"
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "Only the sage knows when to advance and when to retreat, when to survive and when to perish, and never loses the right path."

sentences.zh: 」蓋進有退之義，存有亡之機，得有喪之理，為陛下惜者此也。

translations.literal: For advance carries the meaning of retreat; survival conceals the occasion of perdition; gain contains the principle of loss—it is this that I would have Your Majesty cherish."
translations.idiomatic: Advance already holds retreat within it; survival already holds ruin within it; gain already holds loss within it. That is what I urge Your Majesty to keep in mind."

sentences.zh: 傅曰：「知足不辱，知止不殆。

translations.literal: The Master says: "To know sufficiency is not to be disgraced; to know when to stop is not to come to peril."
translations.idiomatic: Laozi says, "He who knows when he has enough will not suffer shame; he who knows when to stop will not come to harm."

sentences.zh: 」陛下威名功烈既雲足矣，拓地開疆亦可止矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's martial renown and achievements are already more than sufficient; expanding territory and extending frontiers may also be halted.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's fame and feats of arms are already more than enough. The time has come to stop opening new lands and pushing the borders further.

sentences.zh: 邊夷醜種，不足待以仁義，責以常禮，古者以禽魚畜之。

translations.literal: The vile breeds among the frontier barbarians are not fit to be treated with benevolence and righteousness or held to ordinary rites; the ancients kept them like birds and fish in captivity.
translations.idiomatic: These coarse tribes along the frontier are not men to whom one owes the full measure of benevolence and ritual propriety. The ancients regarded them as one might birds and fish—creatures to be kept, not equals to be cultivated.

sentences.zh: 必絕其類，恐獸窮則搏，苟救其死。

translations.literal: If one must exterminate their kind entirely, one need only fear that when beasts are driven to desperation they will fight back; merely spare them and allow them to live.
translations.idiomatic: If you must wipe out their kind to the last, you need only fear that cornered beasts will turn and fight. Better simply to spare their lives.

sentences.zh: 且陛下每決死罪，必三覆五奏，進疏食，停音樂，以人命之重為感動也。

translations.literal: Moreover, each time Your Majesty passes sentence of death, you invariably review the case three times and report five times, take plain food, and halt music—moved by the gravity of human life.
translations.idiomatic: And yet whenever Your Majesty confirms a capital sentence, you review the case again and again, take frugal meals, and suspend the music of the court—so deeply does the weight of a human life move you.

sentences.zh: 今士無一罪，驅之行陣之間，委之鋒鏑之下，使肝腦塗地，老父孤子、寡妻慈母望槥車，抱枯骨，摧心掩泣，其所以變動陰陽，傷害和氣，實天下之痛也。

translations.literal: Now soldiers who have committed no crime are driven into battle formations and cast beneath the clash of blades and arrows, their livers and brains smeared across the ground; old fathers, orphaned sons, widowed wives, and fond mothers watch for the coffin carts, clutch dry bones, and weep with breaking hearts—this upsets the balance of yin and yang, harms the harmonious qi, and is the great agony of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now innocent men are driven into the ranks and sent under the rain of steel, their bodies torn to pieces. Old fathers and orphaned sons, widowed wives and grieving mothers watch for the wagons of the dead, clutching dry bones and weeping until their hearts break. This disturbs heaven and earth, wounds the harmony of the realm, and is a sorrow that falls upon the whole empire.

sentences.zh: 使高麗違失臣節，誅之可也；

translations.literal: If Goguryeo has failed in its duties as a vassal, it may be punished;
translations.idiomatic: If Goguryeo has violated its obligations as a subject state, it may be punished;

sentences.zh: 侵擾百姓，滅之可也；

translations.literal: if it harasses the people, it may be destroyed;
translations.idiomatic: if it plunders and harms the people, it may be destroyed;

sentences.zh: 能為後世患，夷之可也。

translations.literal: if it can become a plague to later ages, it may be wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: if it threatens to become a scourge to future generations, it may be eradicated.

sentences.zh: 今無是三者，而坐敝中國，為舊王雪恥，新羅報仇，非所存小、所損大乎？

translations.literal: Now none of these three conditions apply, yet we sit by and exhaust China, all to avenge an old king's humiliation and settle Silla's grudge—is this not a case of preserving what is small while harming what is great?
translations.idiomatic: Yet none of these three conditions holds today, and still we drain the strength of the Middle Kingdom to avenge an old king's shame and settle a score for Silla. Is this not saving what is petty while ruining what is great?

sentences.zh: 臣願下沛然之詔，許高麗自新，焚陵波之船，罷應募之眾，即臣死骨不朽。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly wishes that you would issue a sweeping edict, permit Goguryeo to reform itself, burn the ships at Lingbo, and disband the conscripted masses—then even this servant's dead bones would know no decay.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to issue a generous edict of amnesty, allow Goguryeo to begin anew, burn the expedition fleet, and send the conscripts home. Then, though I die, my bones will not crumble into dust unredeemed.

sentences.zh: 帝得疏，謂高陽公主曰：「是已危懾，尚能憂吾國事乎！」

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the memorial, he said to Princess Gaoyang: "He is already in mortal peril, yet he can still worry over affairs of state!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor read the memorial, he said to Princess Gaoyang, "The man is already at death's door, and still he troubles himself over the affairs of the realm!"

sentences.zh: 玄齡當國，夙夜勤強，任公竭節，不欲一物失所。

translations.literal: When Xuanling held the reins of state, he toiled day and night with tireless diligence, devoting himself utterly to public duty and unwilling that a single thing should fall out of place.
translations.idiomatic: While Xuanling directed the government, he worked from dawn till late every night, giving himself wholly to public service and allowing nothing, however small, to go neglected.

sentences.zh: 無媢忌，聞人善，若己有之。

translations.literal: Free of envy, when he heard of another's virtue he rejoiced as if it were his own.
translations.idiomatic: He was without jealousy. When he learned of another man's excellence, he delighted in it as though it were his own.

sentences.zh: 明達吏治，而緣飾以文雅，議法處令，務為寬平。

translations.literal: Clear in his mastery of administrative governance, he yet adorned it with refinement and grace; in deliberating on law and issuing orders, he strove always for leniency and fairness.
translations.idiomatic: He understood the arts of administration thoroughly, yet clothed them in learning and elegance. In framing laws and issuing commands, he always sought what was generous and equitable.

sentences.zh: 不以己長望人，取人不求備，雖卑賤皆得盡所能。

translations.literal: He did not measure others by his own strengths, nor did he demand perfection in those he selected; even men of humble station were allowed to give full play to their abilities.
translations.idiomatic: He did not expect others to match his own talents, nor did he require those he employed to be flawless. Even men of low rank were given room to use whatever gifts they possessed.

sentences.zh: 或以事被讓，必稽顙請罪，畏惕，視若無所容。

translations.literal: If he was reproached over some matter, he would invariably prostrate himself and beg forgiveness, trembling with fear as though he had no room to stand.
translations.idiomatic: If he was rebuked for any fault, he would always kowtow and plead guilty, stricken with fear as though he had nowhere on earth to hide.

sentences.zh: 貞觀末年，以譴還第，黃門侍郎褚遂良言於帝曰：「玄齡事君自無所負，不可以一眚便示斥外，非天子任大臣意。

translations.literal: In the final years of the Zhenguan reign, [Xuanling] was rebuked and sent back to his residence. Yellow Gate Assistant Censor Chu Suiliang said to the Emperor: "In serving Your Majesty, Xuanling has never failed in his duty. One small fault should not be grounds to cast him aside—this is not how a Son of Heaven ought to employ his great ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhenguan era, Xuanling was censured and sent home. Yellow Gate Vice Censor Chu Suiliang said to the Emperor, "In his service to you, Xuanling has never been wanting. To dismiss him for a single lapse is not the way a Son of Heaven should treat a chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」帝悟，遽召於家。

translations.literal: The Emperor understood and immediately summoned him from his home.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took his meaning and at once recalled him from his house.

sentences.zh: 後避位不出。

translations.literal: Afterward he declined office and would not come forth.
translations.idiomatic: Later he avoided public office and refused to leave his home.

sentences.zh: 久之，會帝幸芙蓉園觀風俗，玄齡敕子弟汛掃廷堂，曰：「乘輿且臨幸。

translations.literal: After some time, when the Emperor happened to visit Furong Garden to observe local customs, Xuanling ordered his sons and younger relatives to sweep the court and hall, saying, "The imperial carriage will soon arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Some time passed, and when the Emperor came to Furong Garden to observe the ways of the people, Xuanling told his sons and kinsmen to sweep the courtyard and halls, saying, "The imperial carriage is about to arrive."

sentences.zh: 」有頃，帝果幸其第，因載玄齡還宮。

translations.literal: Before long the Emperor did indeed visit his residence and, taking Xuanling with him, returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: A little while later the Emperor did come to his house, and taking Xuanling with him in the carriage, returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝在翠微宮，以司農卿李緯為民部尚書，會有自京師來者，帝曰：「玄齡聞緯為尚書謂何？

translations.literal: When the Emperor was at Cuiwei Palace, he appointed Director of the Directorate of Agriculture Li Wei as Minister of the Ministry of Revenue. When someone arrived from the capital, the Emperor asked, "What did Xuanling say when he heard that Wei had been made Minister?"
translations.idiomatic: While the Emperor was at Cuiwei Palace, he made Li Wei, Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, Minister of Revenue. When a visitor arrived from the capital, the Emperor asked, "What did Xuanling say when he heard that Wei had been appointed Minister?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「惟稱緯好須，無它語。

translations.literal: He replied, "He only said that Wei has a fine beard—nothing else."
translations.idiomatic: The man answered, "He only remarked that Wei has a handsome beard—nothing more."

sentences.zh: 」帝遽改太子詹事。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately changed [Wei's appointment to] Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor at once transferred Wei to the post of Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 帝討遼，玄齡守京師，有男子上急變，玄齡詰狀，曰：「我乃告公。

translations.literal: When the Emperor marched against Liaodong, Xuanling guarded the capital. A man submitted an urgent report [of conspiracy]; Xuanling questioned him, and the man said, "I mean to inform you, my lord."
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor campaigned against Liaodong, Xuanling remained to guard the capital. A man brought an urgent denunciation. Xuanling questioned him, and the man said, "It is you, my lord, whom I mean to accuse."

sentences.zh: 」玄齡驛遣追帝，帝視奏已，斬男子。

translations.literal: Xuanling sent a fast courier after the Emperor. After the Emperor read the memorial, he executed the man.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling dispatched a courier by post to overtake the Emperor. When the Emperor had read the report, he ordered the man beheaded.

sentences.zh: 下詔責曰：「公何不自信！

translations.literal: An edict was issued reproaching [Xuanling]: "Why did you not trust yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed rebuking him: "Why did you not trust yourself!"

sentences.zh: 」其委任類如此。

translations.literal: His entrustment [by the Emperor] was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the measure of trust the Emperor placed in him.

sentences.zh: 治家有法度，常恐諸子驕侈，席勢淩人，乃集古今家誡，書為屏風，令各取一具，曰：「留意於此，足以保躬矣！

translations.literal: In managing his household he maintained strict standards, ever fearing that his sons might grow arrogant and extravagant and rely on their family's power to bully others. He collected admonitions for the family from antiquity to the present, had them written on standing screens, and ordered each [son] to take one, saying, "Keep heed of this—it will be enough to preserve yourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: He ran his household with strict discipline, ever fearing that his sons might grow proud and wasteful and use the family's influence to lord it over others. He gathered family admonitions old and new, had them copied onto standing screens, and gave one to each son, saying, "Keep these words before you, and they will be enough to preserve your lives and honor."

sentences.zh: 漢袁氏累葉忠節，吾心所尚，爾宜師之。

translations.literal: The Yuan clan of Han maintained loyalty and integrity for generations—this is what my heart admires; you should take them as your model.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan family of Han served with loyalty and integrity for generation after generation—that is the example my heart holds dear, and the one you should follow.

sentences.zh: 」子遺直嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yizhi succeeded [to the title].
translations.idiomatic: His son Yizhi succeeded to the estate and title.

sentences.zh: 子 遺愛

translations.literal: Son: Yi'ai
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yi'ai

sentences.zh: 次子遺愛，誕率無學，有武力。

translations.literal: The second son, Yi'ai, was dissolute and crude, without learning, but possessed martial strength.
translations.idiomatic: The second son, Yi'ai, was reckless and unlettered, a man of coarse manners, though he had physical courage.

sentences.zh: 尚高陽公主，為右衛將軍。

translations.literal: He married Princess Gaoyang and served as General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Gaoyang and was appointed General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 公主，帝所愛，故禮與它婿絕。

translations.literal: The princess was a favorite of the Emperor, so the courtesy shown [Yi'ai] was unlike that accorded any other son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was the Emperor's beloved daughter, and so the honors paid to her husband exceeded those given to any other imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 主驕蹇，疾遺直任嫡，遺直懼，讓爵，帝不許。

translations.literal: The princess was arrogant and overbearing; she resented that Yizhi held the position of heir. Yizhi, in fear, offered to yield the noble rank, but the Emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was proud and imperious. She resented that Yizhi, as the eldest son, stood to inherit the family rank. Frightened, Yizhi offered to renounce his claim, but the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 主稍失愛，意怏怏。

translations.literal: The princess gradually lost the Emperor's affection and nursed a sullen discontent.
translations.idiomatic: The princess slowly fell from the Emperor's favor and brooded in bitter resentment.

sentences.zh: 與浮屠辯機亂，帝怒，斬浮屠，殺奴婢數十人，主怨望，帝崩，哭不哀。

translations.literal: She had an illicit affair with the Buddhist monk Bianji. The Emperor was furious: he executed the monk and killed several dozen maidservants. The princess harbored resentment; when the Emperor died, she did not mourn with proper grief.
translations.idiomatic: She entered into an illicit affair with the Buddhist monk Bianji. The Emperor flew into a rage, executed the monk, and put several dozen serving women to death. The princess nursed her grievance, and when the Emperor died she showed no proper sorrow at his passing.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，出遺直汴州刺史，遺愛房州刺史。

translations.literal: In Gaozong's reign, Yizhi was sent out as Prefect of Bianzhou and Yi'ai as Prefect of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong, Yizhi was appointed prefect of Bianzhou and Yi'ai prefect of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 主又誣遺直罪，帝敕長孫無忌鞫治，乃得主與遺愛反狀，遺愛伏誅，主賜死。

translations.literal: The princess again falsely accused Yizhi of crimes. The Emperor ordered Zhangsun Wuji to investigate, whereupon the evidence of the princess's and Yi'ai's conspiracy to rebel was uncovered. Yi'ai was executed; the princess was granted death [ordered to commit suicide].
translations.idiomatic: The princess again lodged false charges against Yizhi. The Emperor commanded Zhangsun Wuji to investigate, and the proof of her and Yi'ai's plot to rebel came to light. Yi'ai was executed, and the princess was ordered to take her own life.

sentences.zh: 遺直以先勳免，貶銅陵尉。

translations.literal: Yizhi was spared on account of his father's earlier merit and was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Tongling.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi was spared because of his father's old service and was demoted to assistant magistrate of Tongling.

sentences.zh: 詔停配享。

translations.literal: An edict stopped [Fang Xuanling's] posthumous sacrifices [at the imperial ancestral temple].
translations.idiomatic: An edict removed Fang Xuanling from the roll of spirits honored at the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 杜如晦

translations.literal: Du Ruhui
translations.idiomatic: Du Ruhui

sentences.zh: 杜如晦，字克明，京兆杜陵人。

translations.literal: Du Ruhui, styled Keming, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ruhui, courtesy name Keming, was a native of Duling in the capital district of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖果，有名周、隋間。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guo was renowned during the Zhou and Sui dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guo had been a man of note in the Northern Zhou and Sui periods.

sentences.zh: 如晦少英爽，喜書，以風流自命，內負大節，臨機輒斷。

translations.literal: Ruhui in youth was spirited and bright, fond of books, and styled himself a man of refinement; inwardly he bore great integrity and, when faced with critical moments, always acted with decisive resolution.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Ruhui was quick and brilliant, devoted to books, and fancied himself a man of cultivated grace. Inwardly he held himself to the highest standards, and when crisis came he always acted with swift, firm decision.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，預吏部選，侍郎高孝基異之，曰：「君當為棟樑用，願保令德。

translations.literal: During the Daye reign of Sui, he participated in the Ministry of Personnel selection. Vice Minister Gao Xiaoji was struck by him and said, "You are fit to serve as a pillar of the state—may you preserve your fine virtue."
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era of Sui he entered the civil service examinations. Vice Minister of Personnel Gao Xiaoji marked him out and said, "You are timber fit to become a pillar of the realm—guard your virtue well."

sentences.zh: 」因補滏陽尉，棄官去。

translations.literal: He was accordingly appointed Assistant Magistrate of Fuyang, but he abandoned the post and left.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon appointed assistant magistrate of Fuyang, but he resigned the post and departed.

sentences.zh: 高祖平京師，秦王引為府兵曹參軍，徙陝州總管府長史。

translations.literal: After Gaozu pacified the capital, the Prince of Qin brought him in as a Military Affairs Staff Officer in his princely establishment, and [Ruhui] was transferred to serve as Chief Administrator of the Shaanzhou Area Command headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu secured the capital, the Prince of Qin took him on as a military staff officer in his household, then transferred him to serve as chief administrator of the Shaanzhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時府屬多外遷，王患之。

translations.literal: At that time many members of the princely staff were being transferred to outside posts, and the Prince was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many of the prince's staff were being posted away to outside offices, and the Prince was deeply troubled by the loss.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡曰：「去者雖多，不足吝，如晦王佐才也。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling said, "Though those who have left are many, they are not worth regretting—but Ruhui is a talent fit to assist a king.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling said, "However many have gone, none of them is worth grieving over—but Ruhui is a man born to assist a ruler.

sentences.zh: 大王若終守籓，無所事；

translations.literal: If Your Highness intends ultimately to remain content within your fief, there is nothing [for which you need him];
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness means to remain forever content within your fief, you have no use for him;

sentences.zh: 必欲經營四方，舍如晦無共功者。

translations.literal: but if you mean to strive for dominion over the four quarters, apart from Ruhui there is none with whom you could accomplish it."
translations.idiomatic: but if you mean to win the empire, there is no one else with whom you can achieve it."

sentences.zh: 」王驚曰：「非公言，我幾失之！

translations.literal: The Prince started and said, "But for your words, I would nearly have lost him!"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince started in alarm and said, "Had you not spoken, I would almost have let him slip away!"

sentences.zh: 」因表留幕府。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized to retain [Ruhui] in his staff headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon submitted a memorial asking that Ruhui be kept on in his staff.

sentences.zh: 從征伐，常參帷幄機秘。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince on campaigns and regularly participated in the secret counsels within the command tent.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the Prince on campaign and was constantly present at the secret deliberations within the command tent.

sentences.zh: 方多事，裁處無留，僚屬共才之，莫見所涯。

translations.literal: In a time of many urgent affairs, he rendered decisions without delay; his colleagues together marveled at his talent, and none could see the limits of his capacity.
translations.idiomatic: In those busy years he disposed of business without a moment's delay. His colleagues all recognized his genius, yet none could tell where his abilities ended.

sentences.zh: 進陝東道大行台司勳郎中，封建平縣男，兼文學館學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director in the Bureau of Merits under the Grand Area Command of the Shandong Circuit, enfeoffed as Baron of Pingyi County, and concurrently made a Scholar of the Hall of Literary Studies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Bureau of Merits of the Shandong Grand Area Command, enfeoffed as Baron of Pingyi County, and made a scholar of the Hall of Literary Studies as well.

sentences.zh: 天策府建，為中郎。

translations.literal: When the Celestial Stratagem Command was established, he served as Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Celestial Stratagem Command was created, he served as its commandant.

sentences.zh: 王為皇太子，授左庶子，遷兵部尚書，進封蔡國公，食三千戶，別食益州千三百戶。

translations.literal: When the Prince became Crown Prince, [Ruhui] was appointed Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent, then transferred to Minister of the Ministry of War, advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of the State of Cai with an estate of three thousand households, and granted a separate estate in Yizhou of one thousand three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince became crown prince, Ruhui was made Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent, then transferred to Minister of War, raised to Duke of Cai with an income of three thousand households, and granted a separate estate of thirteen hundred households in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校侍中，攝吏部尚書，總監東宮兵，進位尚書右僕射，仍領選。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was made Acting Chief Counselor, acting Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, placed in overall charge of the Eastern Palace troops, promoted to Vice Minister of the Right of the Department of State Affairs, and retained charge of official selection.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made acting chief counselor and acting minister of personnel, placed in overall command of the Eastern Palace troops, promoted to Vice Minister of the Right of the Department of State Affairs, and kept charge of official appointments.

sentences.zh: 與玄齡共筦朝政，引士賢者，下不肖，鹹得職，當時浩然歸重。

translations.literal: Together with Xuanling he jointly managed court and government, elevated worthy men and removed the unworthy—all found their proper places, and the age wholeheartedly looked up to them.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Xuanling he governed the court, advancing the worthy and dismissing the unfit until every man stood in his proper place. The whole age looked to them with reverence.

sentences.zh: 監察御史陳師合上《拔士論》，謂一人不可總數職，陰剴諷如晦等。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Chen Shihe submitted a "Discourse on Selecting Scholars," arguing that one man should not hold numerous offices at once—a veiled, cutting satire aimed at Ruhui and his colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censor Chen Shihe submitted a memorial entitled "On Selecting Scholars," arguing that one man should not hold many offices at once—a veiled attack aimed at Ruhui and the others.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「玄齡、如晦不以勳舊進，特其才可與治天下者，師合欲以此離間吾君臣邪？

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Xuanling and Ruhui did not advance on the strength of old merit alone—it is solely because their talent qualifies them to govern all under Heaven. Does Shihe wish to use this to drive a wedge between ruler and ministers?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Xuanling and Ruhui were not promoted merely as old companions in arms, but because their abilities qualify them to govern the realm. Does Shihe mean to use this to drive a wedge between me and my ministers?"

sentences.zh: 」斥嶺表。

translations.literal: [Shihe] was banished to the region south of the Five Ridges.
translations.idiomatic: Shihe was exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 久之，以疾辭職，詔給常俸就第，醫候之使道相屬。

translations.literal: After some time, [Ruhui], citing illness, resigned his office. An edict granted him his regular salary at home, and envoys bearing physicians followed one after another along the road.
translations.idiomatic: After a time Ruhui resigned on grounds of illness. An edict allowed him to keep his regular salary at home, and physicians sent from court followed one after another to his door.

sentences.zh: 會病力，詔皇太子就問，帝親至其家，撫之梗塞。

translations.literal: When his illness grew severe, an edict ordered the Crown Prince to visit and inquire after him; the Emperor himself came to his home and, stroking him, was choked with grief.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness turned grave, the crown prince was sent to visit him by imperial command. The Emperor himself came to his house, and as he stroked Ruhui's hand, grief closed his throat and he could not speak.

sentences.zh: 及未亂，擢其子左千牛構兼尚舍奉禦。

translations.literal: Before his faculties failed, [the Emperor] promoted his son Gou, a Left Thousand-Bull [Guard], to concurrent Palace Supply Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before the end came, the Emperor promoted his son Gou, an officer of the Left Thousand-Bull Guard, to the additional post of Palace Supply Attendant.

sentences.zh: 薨，年四十六，帝哭為慟，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He died at forty-six. The Emperor wept in deepest grief and posthumously granted him the honorific of Grand Master with the Golden Grande Badge.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-six. The Emperor mourned him with bitter grief and posthumously granted him the rank of Grand Master of the Palace with the privilege of an independent office.

sentences.zh: 及葬，加司空，諡曰成。

translations.literal: At his burial he was further granted the title of Minister of Works, with the posthumous name Cheng ("Accomplished").
translations.idiomatic: At his burial he was further honored as Minister of Works, with the posthumous name Cheng, "Accomplished."

sentences.zh: 手詔虞世南勒文於碑，使言君臣痛悼意。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally commanded Yu Shinan to inscribe the stele text, ordering that it convey the grief shared between ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor himself commanded Yu Shinan to compose the inscription for his stele, instructing him to set down the sorrow felt between lord and minister.

sentences.zh: 它日，食瓜美，輟其半奠焉。

translations.literal: On another day, [the Emperor] was eating melon and found it delicious; he set aside half as an offering before [Ruhui's spirit].
translations.idiomatic: On another day, while eating melon, he found it unusually sweet and set half of it aside as an offering before Ruhui's spirit.

sentences.zh: 嘗賜玄齡黃銀帶，曰：「如晦與公同輔朕，今獨見公。

translations.literal: Once he bestowed upon Xuanling a yellow-silver belt, saying, "Ruhui assisted me just as you did—yet now I see you alone."
translations.idiomatic: Once he gave Xuanling a belt of yellow silver, saying, "Ruhui served me at your side, yet now I see only you."

sentences.zh: 」泫然流淚曰：「世傅黃銀鬼神畏之。

translations.literal: With tears streaming, [the Emperor] said, "It is handed down through the ages that ghosts and spirits fear yellow silver."
translations.idiomatic: Tears running down his face, he said, "Tradition holds that ghosts and spirits fear yellow silver."

sentences.zh: 」更取金帶，遣玄齡送其家。

translations.literal: He took instead a gold belt and sent Xuanling to deliver it to Ruhui's household.
translations.idiomatic: He chose a gold belt instead and sent Xuanling to carry it to Ruhui's home.

sentences.zh: 後忽夢如晦若平生，明日為玄齡言之，敕所禦饌往祭。

translations.literal: Later he suddenly dreamed of Ruhui as in life; the next day he told Xuanling of it and commanded that food from the imperial kitchen be sent as sacrificial offering.
translations.idiomatic: Later he dreamed suddenly of Ruhui as though he were still alive. The next day he told Xuanling of the dream and ordered food from the imperial kitchen sent as a sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 明年之祥，遣尚宮勞問妻子，國府官佐亦不之罷，恩禮無少衰。

translations.literal: On the first anniversary of his death, he dispatched the Director of Palace Women to convey consolation to Ruhui's wife and children; the officials and staff of the princely establishment were not dismissed either—imperial favor and courtesy diminished not in the least.
translations.idiomatic: On the first anniversary of Ruhui's death, he sent the Director of Palace Women to inquire after his wife and children. The officials and retainers of Ruhui's household were not dismissed either, and the imperial kindness shown them did not fade in the least.

sentences.zh: 後詔功臣世襲，追贈密州刺史，徙國萊。

translations.literal: Later, when an edict granted hereditary honors to meritorious officials, [Ruhui] was posthumously granted the post of Prefect of Mizhou and his noble domain was transferred to the State of Lai.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when an edict granted hereditary honors to the founding ministers, Ruhui was posthumously made prefect of Mizhou and his noble fief was transferred to the State of Lai.

sentences.zh: 方為相時，天下新定，台閣制度，憲物容典，率二人討裁。

translations.literal: When they served as chancellors, the empire had only just been pacified; the institutions of the central administration, the standards of governmental forms, and the ritual protocols—all were largely drafted and settled by the two of them.
translations.idiomatic: When they served as chief ministers, the realm had only just been settled. The structure of the central government, the forms of official business, and the standards of court ritual were largely shaped and fixed by the two of them.

sentences.zh: 每議事帝所，玄齡必曰：「非如晦莫籌之。

translations.literal: Whenever matters were deliberated in the Emperor's presence, Xuanling would invariably say, "No one but Ruhui can devise the plan for this."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a question was debated before the Emperor, Xuanling would always say, "No one but Ruhui can work out the strategy for this."

sentences.zh: 」及如晦至，卒用玄齡策也。

translations.literal: And when Ruhui arrived, it would in the end be Xuanling's strategy that was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Ruhui came, the plan adopted in the end was always Xuanling's.

sentences.zh: 蓋如晦長於斷，而玄齡善謀，兩人深相知，故能同心濟謀，以佐佑帝，當世語良相，必曰房、杜雲。

translations.literal: For Ruhui excelled at decision, while Xuanling excelled at planning; the two understood each other deeply and therefore could join minds to advance their counsel and support the Emperor—in their day, whenever men spoke of great ministers, they were sure to say "Fang and Du."
translations.idiomatic: Ruhui's strength lay in decisive judgment, Xuanling's in devising strategy. Knowing each other through and through, they worked as one mind to counsel and support the throne. In their time, whenever men spoke of great ministers, they said simply, "Fang and Du."

sentences.zh: 構位慈州刺史。

translations.literal: [Gou] held the post of Prefect of Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gou served as prefect of Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 次子荷，性暴詭不循法，尚城陽公主，官至尚乘奉禦，封襄陽郡公。

translations.literal: The second son, He, was by nature violent, deceitful, and did not follow the law. He married the Princess of Chengyang, reached the office of Groom of the Imperial Carriage, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His second son, He, was violent, cunning, and scornful of the law. He married the Princess of Chengyang, rose to Groom of the Imperial Carriage, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 承乾謀反，荷曰：「琅邪顏利仁善星數，言天有變，宜建大事，陛下當為太上皇。

translations.literal: When Chengqian plotted rebellion, He said: "Yan Liren of Langye is skilled at astrology. He says Heaven has changed, that a great act should be undertaken, and Your Highness should become Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengqian plotted rebellion, He said, "Yan Liren of Langye is skilled in astronomy and says Heaven's signs demand a bold stroke — Your Highness should take the throne and make the emperor Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 請稱疾，上必臨問，可以得志。

translations.literal: Please feign illness; the emperor will surely come in person to inquire, and you may achieve your aim."
translations.idiomatic: Feign illness — the emperor is sure to come in person to inquire, and then you will have your chance."

sentences.zh: 」及敗，坐誅。

translations.literal: When the plot failed, he was executed for his involvement.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot failed, he was executed for his role in it.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，意象軒驁。

translations.literal: Facing execution, his bearing was lofty and proud.
translations.idiomatic: At the execution, he faced death with an air of bold pride.

sentences.zh: 構以累貶死嶺表。

translations.literal: Gou was demoted through accumulated guilt and died in Lingbiao.
translations.idiomatic: Gou was demoted on accumulated charges and died in exile beyond the Ling mountains.

sentences.zh: 弟 楚客

translations.literal: Younger brother: Chuke
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Chuke

sentences.zh: 如晦弟楚客，少尚奇節，與叔父淹皆沒于王世充。

translations.literal: Ruhui's younger brother Chuke, in youth admired remarkable integrity. He and his uncle Yan were both captives of Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Ruhui's younger brother Chuke admired bold integrity from youth. He and his uncle Yan both fell into Wang Shichong's hands as captives.

sentences.zh: 淹與如晦有隙，譖其兄殺之，並囚楚客瀕死。

translations.literal: Yan had a rift with Ruhui and slandered him, having his elder brother killed; he also imprisoned Chuke near to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yan bore a grudge against Ruhui and slandered him until his elder brother was executed. He also imprisoned Chuke and left him near death.

sentences.zh: 世充平，淹當誅。

translations.literal: When Shichong was pacified, Yan was due to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong was overthrown, Yan was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 楚客請於如晦，不許。

translations.literal: Chuke pleaded with Ruhui on Yan's behalf; he did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke pleaded with Ruhui to spare Yan, but Ruhui refused.

sentences.zh: 楚客曰：「叔殘兄，今兄又棄叔，門內幾盡，豈不痛哉！

translations.literal: Chuke said: "Our uncle cruelly killed our brother; now our brother in turn abandons our uncle — the family is nearly destroyed within our gates. Is this not painful!"
translations.idiomatic: Chuke said, "Our uncle destroyed our brother cruelly, and now our brother would abandon our uncle — the household is nearly wiped out. How can that not grieve us!"

sentences.zh: 」如晦感悟，請之高祖，得釋。

translations.literal: Ruhui was moved and understood; he petitioned Gaozu, and Yan was released.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by this, Ruhui pleaded with Gaozu, and Yan was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 方建成難作，楚客遁舍嵩山。

translations.literal: Just as the crisis over Jiancheng arose, Chuke fled and hid on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis over Crown Prince Jiancheng erupted, Chuke took refuge on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，召為給事中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan, he was summoned to serve as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 4, he was recalled to serve as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「君居山似之矣，謂非宰相不起，渠然邪？

translations.literal: Taizong said: "You lived on the mountain as if it were so — saying you would not rise unless made chancellor. Was it really so?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "You lived on the mountain as though you would not serve unless made chancellor — was that truly the case?"

sentences.zh: 夫走遠者自近，人不恤無官，患才不副。

translations.literal: Those who go far eventually draw near on their own; men need not worry about lacking an office — what they fear is that talent does not match the post.
translations.idiomatic: Those who withdraw far eventually return of their own accord. A man need not fret over lacking office; what matters is whether his talents fit the task.

sentences.zh: 而兄與我異支一心者，爾當如兄事吾而輔我。

translations.literal: Your elder brother and I, though of different surname branches, were of one mind. You should serve me as your brother did and assist me."
translations.idiomatic: Your brother and I, though not kin, were of one mind. Serve me as he did, and aid me."

sentences.zh: 」楚客頓首謝，因擢為中郎將。

translations.literal: Chuke kowtowed in thanks and was thereupon promoted to Captain of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke kowtowed in thanks and was promoted to Captain of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 每入直，盡夕不釋杖，帝知而勞之，進蒲州刺史，政有能名，徙瀛州。

translations.literal: Each time he entered duty, he held his staff all night without releasing it. The emperor knew and commended him, advancing him to Prefect of Puzhou. His administration gained a reputation for capability, and he was transferred to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he was on overnight palace duty, he kept his staff in hand until dawn without letting go. The emperor learned of this and commended him, promoting him to prefect of Puzhou, where he earned a name for capable rule before being moved to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 後為魏王府長史，遷工部尚書，攝府事，以威肅聞。

translations.literal: Later he served as Chief Administrator of the Prince of Wei's household, was transferred to Minister of Works, and managed the princely residence affairs, becoming known for stern authority.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as chief administrator of the Prince of Wei's household, rose to Minister of Works while acting on the prince's behalf, and became known for his firm, stern manner.

sentences.zh: 揣帝意薄承乾，乃為王諧媚用事臣，數言王聰睿可為嗣，人或以聞，帝隱恚。

translations.literal: Divining that the emperor's regard for Chengqian had cooled, he ingratiated himself with those in power around the prince and repeatedly said the prince was clever and worthy to succeed. Some reported this, and the emperor secretly resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Sensing the emperor's cooling toward Chengqian, he flattered the prince's influential retainers and repeatedly praised the prince's intelligence and fitness to succeed. Word reached the emperor, who kept his anger hidden.

sentences.zh: 及王貶爵，暴其罪，以如晦功免死，廢於家，終虔化令。

translations.literal: When the prince was stripped of rank, his crimes were exposed. On account of Ruhui's merit, Chuke was spared death but was disgraced and confined at home, ending as magistrate of Qianhua.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was demoted, his crimes were made public. Because of Ruhui's past service, Chuke was spared death but cashiered to live at home, ending his days as magistrate of Qianhua.

sentences.zh: 叔父 淹

translations.literal: Uncle: Yan
translations.idiomatic: Uncle: Yan

sentences.zh: 淹，字執禮，材辯多聞，有美名。

translations.literal: Yan, styled Zhili, was talented in debate and widely learned, with a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, styled Zhili, was gifted in argument and widely learned, and enjoyed an excellent reputation.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，與其友韋福嗣謀曰：「上好用隱民，蘇威以隱者召，得美官。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang of Sui, he plotted with his friend Wei Fusi, saying: "The emperor likes recluses. Su Wei was summoned as a hermit and obtained a fine office."
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang reign, he schemed with his friend Wei Fusi, saying, "The emperor favors men in retirement — Su Wei was recruited as a recluse and won a fine appointment."

sentences.zh: 」乃共入太白山，為不仕者。

translations.literal: Thereupon they together entered Mount Taibai and lived as men who did not serve.
translations.idiomatic: So the two withdrew together to Mount Taibai and lived as recluses.

sentences.zh: 文帝惡之，謫戍江表。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen disapproved and banished them to guard duty in Jiangbiao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen took offense and banished them for frontier service in the south.

sentences.zh: 赦還，高孝基為雍州司馬，薦授承奉郎，擢累御史中丞。

translations.literal: After amnesty and return, Gao Xiaoji was Prefectural Secretary of Yongzhou; he recommended Yan, who was appointed Gentlemen for Reception, then repeatedly promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After they were pardoned and returned, Gao Xiaoji, as Yongzhou secretary, recommended him for appointment as Gentlemen for Reception, and he rose through successive promotions to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 王世充僭號，署少吏部，頗親近用事。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong usurped the title, Yan was appointed Vice Minister of the Civil Office and became quite close to those in power.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong declared himself emperor, Yan was made vice minister of the civil office and grew close to those who wielded power.

sentences.zh: 洛陽平，不得調，欲往事隱太子。

translations.literal: When Luoyang was pacified, he could not obtain an appointment and wished to go serve the Hidden Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell, he could find no post and wished to enter the service of the Hidden Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 時封倫領選，以諗房玄齡，玄齡恐失之，白秦王，引為天策府兵曹參軍、文學館學士。

translations.literal: At that time Feng Lun oversaw selection; he informed Fang Xuanling. Xuanling feared losing him, reported to the Prince of Qin, and brought Yan in as Military Affairs Officer of the Heavenly Strategies Office and a Literary Institute scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Lun then held the appointment portfolio and tipped off Fang Xuanling, who feared losing so able a man, reported to the Prince of Qin, and secured Yan as military affairs officer of the Heavenly Strategies Office and a scholar of the Literary Institute.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴，賦詩尤工，賜銀鐘。

translations.literal: Once while attending a banquet, his composed verse was especially fine, and he was granted a silver bell.
translations.idiomatic: On one banquet occasion his verse was especially fine, and the prince rewarded him with a silver bell.

sentences.zh: 慶州總管楊文幹反，辭連太子，歸罪淹及王珪、韋挺，並流越巂，王知其誣，餉黃金三百兩。

translations.literal: When Yang Wengan, regional commander of Qingzhou, rebelled, testimony implicated the crown prince. Blame was assigned to Yan, Wang Gui, and Wei Ting, who were all exiled to Yuexi. The prince knew this was a frame-up and sent them three hundred taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Wengan, military commissioner of Qingzhou, rebelled, testimony implicated the crown prince. Yan, Wang Gui, and Wei Ting were blamed and exiled to Yuexi. The Prince of Qin knew they had been falsely implicated and sent them three hundred taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，召為御史大夫，封安吉郡公，食四百戶。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Yan was summoned as Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed as Duke of Anji Commandery, with an income of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong ascended the throne, he recalled Yan as Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed him as Duke of Anji, and granted him an income of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 淹建言諸司文桉稽期，請以御史檢促。

translations.literal: Yan proposed that each office's paperwork be checked for deadlines, requesting that censors supervise and press them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan proposed that censors be assigned to inspect each office's files for tardiness and enforce deadlines.

sentences.zh: 太宗以問僕射封倫，倫曰：「設官各以其事治，御史劾不法，而索桉求疵，是太苛，且侵官。

translations.literal: Taizong asked the Vice Premier Feng Lun. Lun said: "Offices are established so each may govern its own affairs. Censors impeach unlawfulness; to search files for flaws is too harsh and moreover an encroachment on other officials' duties."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong consulted Vice Premier Feng Lun, who replied, "Every office has its own sphere — censors should punish violations, not hunt through files for pretexts. That would be excessively harsh and an invasion of others' jurisdiction."

sentences.zh: 」淹嘿然。

translations.literal: Yan was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan fell silent.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何不申執？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Why not argue your case?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Why did you not press your point?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「倫所引國大體，臣伏其議，又何言？

translations.literal: He replied: "What Lun cited concerns the great principles of the state; I submit to his argument — what more can I say?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Lord Feng spoke to the state's larger principles; I accept his view. What further case could I make?"

sentences.zh: 」帝悅，以資博練，帝敕東宮儀典簿最悉聽淹裁訂。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and considered his learning broad and practiced. The emperor ordered that the Eastern Palace's ceremonial regulations and ledgers be entirely entrusted to Yan for revision.
translations.idiomatic: Pleased, the emperor judged him broadly seasoned in affairs and ordered Yan to revise all ceremonial regulations and ledgers of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校吏部尚書，參豫朝政。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Acting Minister of the Civil Office and participated in deliberating state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting Minister of the Civil Office and took part in governing.

sentences.zh: 所薦贏四十人，後皆知名。

translations.literal: Of those he recommended, more than forty later became well known.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty of those he recommended later rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 嘗白郅懷道可用，帝問狀。

translations.literal: He once reported that Chi Huaidao was usable; the emperor asked for particulars.
translations.idiomatic: He once recommended Chi Huaidao as worthy of appointment, and the emperor asked for particulars.

sentences.zh: 淹曰：「懷道及隋時位吏部主事，方煬帝幸江都，群臣迎阿，獨懷道執不可。

translations.literal: Yan said: "When Huaidao served in Sui as chief clerk in the Ministry of Civil Office, just as Emperor Yang visited Jiangdu, the officials all flattered and agreed — only Huaidao steadfastly objected."
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "When Huaidao was chief clerk in the Ministry of Civil Appointments under the Sui, as Emperor Yang moved to Jiangdu the courtiers all rushed to flatter him — Huaidao alone stood firm in opposition."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿時何雲？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What did you say at the time?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What did you say at the time?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「臣與眾。

translations.literal: He said: "I went with the crowd."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I sided with the majority."

sentences.zh: 」帝折曰：「事君有犯無隱，卿直懷道者，何不讜言？

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him: "Serving a ruler requires remonstrance without concealment — you approve of Huaidao, so why not speak forthrightly?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reproved him: "Serving a ruler means remonstrating without hiding anything — if you truly thought Huaidao right, why did you not speak out boldly?"

sentences.zh: 」謝曰：「臣位下，又顧諫不從，徒死無益。

translations.literal: He apologized: "My rank was low, and I feared that if remonstrance went unheeded, death would be in vain."
translations.idiomatic: He apologized, "My rank was too low, and I feared remonstrance would go unheeded and my death would serve no purpose."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「內以君不足諫，尚何仕？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If inwardly you thought the ruler unworthy of remonstrance, why still serve?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If you inwardly thought the ruler beyond remonstrance, why remain in office at all?"

sentences.zh: 食隋粟忘隋事，忠乎？

translations.literal: Eating Sui grain yet forgetting Sui affairs — is that loyalty?
translations.idiomatic: To eat the Sui state's grain yet forget the Sui state's affairs — is that loyalty?

sentences.zh: 」因顧群臣：「公等謂何？

translations.literal: He then turned to the officials: "What do you gentlemen say?"
translations.idiomatic: He turned to the assembled ministers: "What do you say?"

sentences.zh: 」王珪曰：「比干諫而死，孔子稱仁，泄冶諫亦死，則曰：'民之多僻，無自立辟。

translations.literal: Wang Gui said: "Bi Gan remonstrated and died; Confucius praised his humanity. Xie Zhi remonstrated and also died, yet Confucius said: 'When the people have many crooked ways, do not erect a standard of your own.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui said, "Confucius praised Bi Gan's humanity when he remonstrated and died. Yet when Xie Zhi remonstrated and was killed, Confucius said, 'When the people have many crooked ways, do not set yourself up as upright.'

sentences.zh: '祿重責深，從古則然。

translations.literal: Heavy salary brings deep responsibility — it has been so since antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Great salary carries heavy responsibility — that has been true since antiquity."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「卿在隋不諫，宜置。

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said: "You did not remonstrate under the Sui — that may be excused."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and said, "Your failure to remonstrate under the Sui may be forgiven."

sentences.zh: 世充親任，胡不言？
