translations.literal: Shichong favored and trusted you — why did you not speak up?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shichong trusted you closely — why did you say nothing then?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「固嘗言，不見用。

translations.literal: He replied: "I did speak, but was not heeded."
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "I did speak, but was not heeded."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「世充愎諫飾非，卿若何而免？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Shichong was obstinate in rejecting remonstrance and glossed over faults — if so, how did you escape?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Shichong was obstinate, rejected counsel, and covered his errors — if so, how did you survive?"

sentences.zh: 」淹辭窮不得對。

translations.literal: Yan's arguments were exhausted and he could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had no answer left.

sentences.zh: 帝勉曰：「今任卿已，可有諫未？

translations.literal: The emperor encouraged him: "Now that I have employed you, have you any remonstrance to offer?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then pressed him: "Now that you serve in office, do you have any remonstrance to offer?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「顧死無隱。

translations.literal: He answered: "I shall look to death without concealment."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I intend to remonstrate without concealment even at the cost of my life."

sentences.zh: 」貞觀二年疾，帝為臨問。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan he fell ill; the emperor personally visited to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 2 he fell ill, and the emperor visited him in person.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書右僕射，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given the title of Right Vice Premier; his posthumous name was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Right Vice Premier, with the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 始，淹典二職，貴重於朝矣，而亡清白名，獲譏當世。

translations.literal: At first Yan held two posts and was greatly honored at court, yet he left no reputation for integrity and was ridiculed in his own time.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yan held two major posts and stood high at court, he never earned a name for integrity and was criticized in his own day.

sentences.zh: 子敬同襲爵，官至鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: His son Jingtong inherited the title and reached the post of Chamberlain for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingtong inherited the title and rose to Chamberlain for Dependencies.

sentences.zh: 五世孫 元穎

translations.literal: Fifth-generation descendant: Yuanying
translations.idiomatic: Fifth-generation descendant: Yuanying

sentences.zh: 敬宗驕僻不君，元穎每欲中帝意以固幸，乃巧索珍異獻之，踵相躡於道，百工造作無程，斂取苛重，至削軍食以助裒畜。

translations.literal: Jingzong was arrogant and perverse toward the ruler. Yuanying, wishing always to hit the emperor's wishes to secure favor, cleverly sought rare and exotic items to present. They followed one another on the road in succession. Craftsmen worked without limit; levies were harsh and heavy, reaching the point of cutting military rations to aid accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong was arrogant and ungovernable. To keep the emperor's favor, Yuanying constantly sought rare treasures to present, until tribute convoys crowded the roads one after another. Artisans worked without limit, exactions grew cruel, and he even cut army rations to feed his hoarding.

sentences.zh: 又給與不時，戎人寒饑，乃仰足蠻徼。

translations.literal: Moreover stipends were not paid on time; frontier people suffered cold and hunger and had to look to the barbarian borderlands for bare subsistence.
translations.idiomatic: Pay arrived irregularly; frontier troops went cold and hungry and scraped a living from the tribal marches.

sentences.zh: 於是人人咨苦，反為蠻內覘，戎備不修。

translations.literal: Thereupon everyone complained in misery; they instead became spies for the barbarians within, and frontier defenses were not maintained.
translations.idiomatic: The men groaned in misery, some turned informants for the tribes, and frontier defenses fell into neglect.

sentences.zh: 大和三年，南詔乘虛襲戎、巂等州，諸屯聞賊至，輒潰，戍者為鄉導，遂入成都。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dahe, Nanzhao seized the opportunity to raid Rong, Qian, and other prefectures. At every post, when word came that bandits had arrived, troops scattered at once; garrison soldiers served as guides, and the invaders entered Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In Dahe 3, Nanzhao struck at a moment of weakness and raided Rong, Qian, and neighboring prefectures. Garrisons broke and fled at the first report of the enemy, local defenders served as guides, and the invaders marched into Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 已傅城，元穎尚不知，乃率左右嬰牙城以守。

translations.literal: The enemy had already reached the walls; Yuanying still did not know. He then led his attendants to hold fast within the inner citadel.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy was already at the walls before Yuanying knew anything of it; he then gathered his personal staff and clung to the inner citadel to defend it.

sentences.zh: 賊大掠，焚郛郭，殘之，留數日去，蜀之寶貨、工巧、子女盡矣。

translations.literal: The bandits looted on a great scale, burned the outer city, ravaged it, and after several days departed. Shu's treasures, artisans, and women and children were all gone.
translations.idiomatic: The invaders looted freely, burned the outer city, ravaged what remained, and withdrew after several days, leaving Shu's treasures, craftsmen, and people stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 初，元穎計迫，將挺身走，會救至乃止。

translations.literal: At first Yuanying, in his extremity, planned to flee by himself; only when relief arrived did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: At first, desperate, Yuanying planned to flee alone, but halted when relief finally came.

sentences.zh: 文宗遣使者臨撫南詔，南詔上言：「蜀人祈我誅虐帥，不能克，請陛下誅之，以謝蜀人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong sent envoys to console Nanzhao. Nanzhao submitted a memorial: "The people of Shu begged us to execute their cruel commander; we could not succeed in that. We ask Your Majesty to execute him to appease the people of Shu."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong sent envoys to soothe Nanzhao. Nanzhao replied, "The people of Shu asked us to kill their cruel governor; we could not do it for them. We ask Your Majesty to execute him and answer to the people of Shu."

sentences.zh: 」由是貶邵州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was demoted to Prefect of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was demoted to prefect of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 議者不厭，斥為循州司馬。

translations.literal: Those who deliberated were not satisfied and expelled him as Prefectural Secretary of Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Critics were still not satisfied and had him banished further as prefectural secretary of Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 官屬崔璜、紇幹巘、盧並悉奪秩，分逐之。

translations.literal: His subordinate officials Cui Huang, Qagan Yan, and Lu Bing all had their ranks stripped and were banished separately.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates Cui Huang, Qagan Yan, and Lu Bing all lost rank and were exiled to separate places.

sentences.zh: 元穎死於貶所，年六十四。

translations.literal: Yuanying died in the place of exile at age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying died in exile at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 將終，表丐贈官，乞歸葬。

translations.literal: As he was nearing death, he submitted a memorial begging a posthumous appointment and permission for burial at home.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he petitioned for a posthumous title and permission to be buried at home.

sentences.zh: 詔贈湖州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Prefect of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Prefect of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 元穎與李德裕善，會昌初，德裕當國，因赦令復其官。

translations.literal: Yuanying was on good terms with Li Deyu. At the beginning of Huichang, when Deyu held power, through an amnesty edict his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying had been close to Li Deyu, and when Deyu took power at the start of Huichang, an amnesty restored his office.

sentences.zh: 弟元絳，終太子賓客。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yuanshuo ended as Prefect of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yuanshuo ended his career as Prefect of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 元絳子審權。

translations.literal: Yuanshuo's son Shenquan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshuo's son was Shenquan.

sentences.zh: 六世孫 審權

translations.literal: Sixth-generation descendant: Shenquan
translations.idiomatic: Sixth-generation descendant: Shenquan

sentences.zh: 審權，字殷衡，第進士，辟浙西幕府。

translations.literal: Shenquan, styled Yinheng, placed in the jinshi examination and was summoned to the Zhexi commandery staff.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shenquan, whose courtesy name was Yinheng, passed the jinshi examination and entered service on the staff of the Zhexi commandery.

sentences.zh: 舉拔萃中，為右拾遺。

translations.literal: He placed in the exceptional selection and became Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the exceptional selection examination and was appointed Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 宣宗時，入翰林為學士，累遷兵部侍郎、學士承旨。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuanzong, he entered the Hanlin Academy as Academician and was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of War and Academician Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanzong he entered the Hanlin Academy as an academician, rising in time to Vice Minister of War and Academician Expositor.

sentences.zh: 懿宗立，進同中書門下平章事，再遷門下侍郎，出為鎮海軍節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yizong acceded, he was promoted to Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, then again to Chancellery Vice Minister, and sent out as military commissioner of the Zhenhai Army while retaining the title of Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yizong took the throne, Shenquan was made Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, then Chancellery Vice Minister, and finally sent out as military commissioner of the Zhenhai Army with the same councilor title.

sentences.zh: 龐勳亂徐州，審權與令狐綯、崔鉉連師掎角，饋粟相銜，王師賴濟。

translations.literal: When Pang Xun rebelled at Xuzhou, Shenquan, together with Linghu Tao and Cui Xuan, linked their armies in pincer positions; grain supplies followed one after another, and the imperial army relied on them for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Pang Xun rose in rebellion at Xuzhou, Shenquan joined Linghu Tao and Cui Xuan in a coordinated pincer campaign, sending grain in an unbroken stream on which the imperial forces depended.

sentences.zh: 勳破，進檢校司空，入為尚書左僕射、襄陽郡公。

translations.literal: When Pang was defeated, Shenquan was promoted to Acting Minister of Works, entered the capital as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Pang's defeat he was promoted to Acting Minister of Works, recalled to serve as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 繼領河中、忠武節度使。

translations.literal: He subsequently held the military commissions of Hezhong and Zhongwu in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in succession as military commissioner of Hezhong and of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太師，諡曰德。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title De.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title De.

sentences.zh: 審權清重寡言，性長厚，居翰林最久，終不漏禁近語。

translations.literal: Shenquan was pure, dignified, and sparing of speech; by nature long-suffering and generous; he remained longest in the Hanlin Academy and to the end never leaked confidential inner-court matters.
translations.idiomatic: Shenquan was grave, reserved, and taciturn, with a patient and generous disposition. He served in the Hanlin Academy longer than any of his peers and never once divulged matters of the inner court.

sentences.zh: 在方鎮，視事有常處，要非日入未始就內寢。

translations.literal: In the provinces, he had a fixed place for conducting affairs and, as a rule, would not retire to the inner quarters before the sun had set.
translations.idiomatic: As a regional commissioner he always received petitioners in the same hall and as a rule never withdrew to his private quarters before nightfall.

sentences.zh: 坐必斂衽，常若對大賓客。

translations.literal: When seated he always straightened his robe, as though facing a great guest.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he sat, he kept his robes properly arranged, as if in audience before a distinguished visitor.

sentences.zh: 或晝日少息，則顧直將解簾；

translations.literal: If he rested briefly in the daytime, he would tell the attendant on duty to unhook the curtain;
translations.idiomatic: When he took a short rest during the day, he would instruct the attendant on duty to unhook the curtain;

sentences.zh: 即旁無人，自起徹鉤，手擁簾徐下，乃退。

translations.literal: then, even with no one else present, he would rise himself, remove the hooks, and with his own hands slowly lower the curtain before withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: and even when no one else was present he would rise, take down the hooks himself, and slowly draw the curtain closed before retiring.

sentences.zh: 與杜悰俱位將相，悰先進，故世謂審權為「小杜公」。

translations.literal: He and Du Cong both reached the rank of chief minister and general, but Cong had entered office earlier, so the age called Shenquan the "Little Lord Du."
translations.idiomatic: He and Du Cong both rose to the highest civil and military offices, but because Cong had entered government earlier, contemporaries nicknamed Shenquan "Little Lord Du."

sentences.zh: 七世孫 讓能

translations.literal: Seventh-generation descendant: Rangneng
translations.idiomatic: Seventh-generation descendant: Du Rangneng

sentences.zh: 子讓能，字群懿，擢進士第，從宣武王鐸府為推官，以長安尉為集賢校理。

translations.literal: His son Rangneng, styled Qunyi, placed in the jinshi examination, followed Prince Xuanwu Wang Bo's staff as investigating officer, and from the post of warden of Chang'an became collator in the Hall of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: His son Du Rangneng, courtesy name Qunyi, passed the jinshi examination, served on the staff of Prince Xuanwu Wang Bo as investigating officer, and was promoted from warden of Chang'an to collator in the Hall of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 喪母，以孝聞。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he became known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he won renown for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 又辟劉鄴、牛蔚二府，稍進兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was again summoned to the staffs of Liu Ye and Niu Wei, and was gradually promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recruited to the staffs of Liu Ye and Niu Wei in turn and gradually rose to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 蕭遘領度支，引判度支按。

translations.literal: When Xiao Zou headed the Revenue Bureau, he brought Rangneng in as an assistant for revenue inspection.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Zou took charge of the Revenue Bureau, he appointed Rangneng to assist in revenue audits.

sentences.zh: 僖宗狩蜀，奔謁行在，三遷中書舍人，召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, Rangneng hurried to the mobile court; after three promotions he became Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat, and was summoned as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong took refuge in Shu, Rangneng rushed to the mobile court, rose through three promotions to Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat, and was summoned into the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 方關東兵興，調發綏徠，書詔叢浩，讓能思精敏，凡號令行下，處事值機，無所遺算，帝倚重之。

translations.literal: Just then warfare had broken out in the east, with mobilization, pacification, and winning over of the people; documents and edicts piled in profusion. Rangneng's mind was keen and sharp; in every order issued and every matter handled at the critical moment, nothing was left out of account, and the emperor relied heavily on him.
translations.idiomatic: War had meanwhile erupted in the east, demanding mobilization, conciliation, and the winning over of local powers, while edicts and memorials piled up without end. Rangneng's mind was quick and penetrating; in every decree sent down and every decision taken at a critical juncture, nothing escaped his calculation, and the emperor came to depend on him deeply.

sentences.zh: 從還京師，再遷兵部尚書，封建平縣子。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital, Rangneng was promoted again to Minister of War and enfeoffed as Viscount of Pingping.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to the capital, Rangneng was promoted again to Minister of War and enfeoffed as Viscount of Pingping.

sentences.zh: 李克用兵至，帝夜出鳳翔，蒼黃無知者。

translations.literal: When Li Keyong's army arrived, the emperor fled Fengxiang by night, and in the confusion no one knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Keyong's forces approached, the emperor slipped out of Fengxiang by night, and in the panic almost no one knew he had gone.

sentences.zh: 讓能方直，徒步從十餘里，得遺馬，褫紳為靮乘之。

translations.literal: Rangneng was then on upright duty; he followed on foot for more than ten li, found a stray horse, stripped his official sash to use as a bridle, and mounted it.
translations.idiomatic: Rangneng happened to be on duty at the time. He followed on foot for more than ten li, found an abandoned horse, tore off his sash to serve as a bridle, and rode after the emperor.

sentences.zh: 硃玫兵逼乘輿，帝走寶雞，獨讓能從。

translations.literal: When Zhu Mei's troops pressed upon the imperial carriage, the emperor fled to Baoji, and Rangneng alone followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Mei's soldiers closed in on the imperial train, the emperor fled to Baoji with only Rangneng still at his side.

sentences.zh: 翌日，孔緯等乃至。

translations.literal: The next day Kong Wei and the others finally arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the following day did Kong Wei and the others catch up.

sentences.zh: 俄而進狩梁。

translations.literal: Before long the court proceeded on expedition to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the court moved on toward Liang.

sentences.zh: 是時棧道為山南石君涉所毀，天子間關嶮澀，讓能未嘗暫去側。

translations.literal: At that time the plank road had been destroyed by Shi Junshe of Shannan; the Son of Heaven's journey through perilous passes was arduous, yet Rangneng never for a moment left his side.
translations.idiomatic: The plank roads had by then been wrecked by Shi Junshe of Shannan, and the emperor's passage through the treacherous mountain routes was grueling, yet Rangneng never once left his side.

sentences.zh: 帝勞曰：「朕失道，再遺宗廟。

translations.literal: The emperor consoled him, saying: "I have lost the Way and twice abandoned the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him, saying, "I have lost the Way and twice forsaken the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 方艱難時，卿不少舍朕，蓋古所謂忠於所事邪！

translations.literal: In this time of hardship you did not for a moment leave me—is this not what the ancients called loyalty to one's charge?"
translations.idiomatic: In our darkest hour you never once left me—is this not what the ancients meant by loyalty to one's charge?"

sentences.zh: 」讓能頓首曰：「臣世蒙國厚恩，陛下不以臣不肖，使扞牧圉，臨難苟免，臣之恥也。

translations.literal: Rangneng bowed his head and said: "Your subject's family has for generations received the state's deep grace. Your Majesty did not deem your subject unworthy and made him guard the ruler as a shepherd guards his flock; to seek escape in a crisis would be your subject's shame."
translations.idiomatic: Rangneng kowtowed and replied, "My family has for generations received the deepest favor of the state. Your Majesty did not despise me for my inadequacy and entrusted me to stand guard over you as a shepherd guards his flock. To save myself in a moment of peril would be my disgrace."

sentences.zh: 」帝次褒中，擢兵部侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When the emperor halted at Baozhong, he promoted Rangneng to Vice Minister of War and Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Baozhong, he promoted Rangneng to Vice Minister of War and Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 于時，嗣襄王煴即偽位，強籓大鎮附者已十八，貢賦不輸行在，無以備賞勞，衛兵往往乏食，君臣搏手無它策。

translations.literal: At that time the Succession Prince of Xiang, Li Yun, had assumed a false throne; powerful provinces and great commanderies that had joined him already numbered eighteen. Tribute and taxes did not reach the mobile court, and there was nothing with which to reward and comfort the troops; the imperial guard often lacked food, and ruler and ministers wrung their hands with no other plan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Yun, the Succession Prince of Xiang, had set up a rival throne, and eighteen powerful provinces and major commanderies had already rallied to him. Tribute no longer reached the mobile court, leaving nothing with which to reward the troops; the palace guard often went hungry, and emperor and ministers could only wring their hands in helplessness.

sentences.zh: 讓能建遣大使入河中，以諭王重榮，重榮果奉詔。

translations.literal: Rangneng proposed sending a chief envoy into Hezhong to instruct Wang Chongrong, and Chongrong indeed obeyed the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Rangneng proposed dispatching a chief envoy to Hezhong to win over Wang Chongrong, and Chongrong did in fact submit to the imperial command.

sentences.zh: 已而京師平，進中書侍郎，徙封襄陽郡公。

translations.literal: Before long the capital was pacified; he was promoted to Chancellery Vice Minister and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the capital was restored to order; he was promoted to Chancellery Vice Minister and his title was changed to Duke of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 官吏多汙偽署，有司皆欲論死，讓能以脅從不足深治，固爭之，多所全貸。

translations.literal: Many officials had served under the false regime; the responsible offices all wished to sentence them to death. Rangneng held that those who had been coerced into following should not be punished severely, and he argued the point firmly, so that many were fully spared.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials had held posts under the puppet regime, and the judicial offices all wanted them put to death. Rangneng insisted that those who had followed under duress should not be punished harshly; he argued the point forcefully and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 昭宗立，進尚書左僕射、晉國公，賜鐵券，累進太尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong acceded, Rangneng was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Duke of Jin, granted an iron certificate of pardon, and promoted in succession to Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong took the throne, Rangneng was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Duke of Jin, granted an iron certificate of pardon, and eventually promoted to Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞守鳳翔，自大順後兵浸強，恃有功，不奉法，朝廷弱，弗能制。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen held Fengxiang; after the Da Shun era his armies grew ever stronger. Relying on his achievements, he did not obey the law, and because the court was weak it could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen held Fengxiang. After the Da Shun era his military power steadily increased; trusting in his past service, he ignored the law, and the enfeebled court could not bring him to heel.

sentences.zh: 會楊復恭走山南，茂貞欲兼有梁、漢，請以師問罪，未報而兵出，帝忿其專，然不得已從之。

translations.literal: When Yang Fugong fled into Shannan, Maozhen wished to seize both Liang and Han and requested permission to lead troops to punish him. Before a reply arrived his army was already on the march; the emperor resented his presumption but had no choice but to acquiesce.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Fugong fled into Shannan, Maozhen sought to annex both Liang and Han and asked leave to march against him. Before any answer came his troops were already moving; the emperor was furious at his arrogance but had no choice but to go along.

sentences.zh: 山南平，詔茂貞領興元、武定，而以徐彥若為鳳翔節度使，分果、閬州隸武定軍。

translations.literal: When Shannan was pacified, an edict made Maozhen military commissioner of Xingyuan and Wuding, while Xu Yanruo was made military commissioner of Fengxiang; Guo and Lang prefectures were placed under the Wuding command.
translations.idiomatic: After Shannan was pacified, Maozhen was ordered to take Xingyuan and Wuding, Xu Yanruo was appointed military commissioner of Fengxiang, and the prefectures of Guo and Lang were transferred to the Wuding command.

sentences.zh: 茂貞怨，不赴鎮，上章語悖慢。

translations.literal: Maozhen resented this, refused to go to his post, and submitted a memorial with insolent and disrespectful language.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen resented the arrangement, refused to take up his new command, and submitted a memorial filled with insolent and disrespectful language.

sentences.zh: 又詒書讓能詆責，以為助守亮為亂，抑忠臣，奪己功，其言醜肆。

translations.literal: He also sent a letter reviling Rangneng, accusing him of abetting Li Shouliang's rebellion, suppressing loyal ministers, and stealing his own achievements; the language was vile and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Rangneng a letter of abuse, charging that he had abetted Li Shouliang's rebellion, suppressed loyal officials, and robbed Maozhen of his due credit—language as foul as it was unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 京師匈懼，日數千人守闕下，候中尉西門重遂出，請與茂貞鳳翔地，為百姓計。

translations.literal: Alarm and fear filled the capital; each day several thousand men waited below the palace gates for the Palace Commandant Xi Gate Chongsui to come out and plead that Fengxiang territory be granted to Maozhen for the sake of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread through the capital. Every day thousands gathered beneath the palace gates, waiting for Palace Commandant Xi Gate Chongsui to emerge and beg that Fengxiang be ceded to Maozhen for the people's sake.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「事出宰相，我無預。

translations.literal: He answered: "The matter comes from the chief minister; I have no part in it."
translations.idiomatic: Chongsui replied, "This is the chief minister's decision; it has nothing to do with me."

sentences.zh: 」茂貞益怨。

translations.literal: Maozhen grew even more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen's resentment only deepened.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，詔讓能計議，且趣調發，經月不就第。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered, ordered Rangneng to deliberate on a plan, and also pressed for mobilization; for a month Rangneng did not return to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, enraged, ordered Rangneng to devise a strategy and pressed urgently for troop mobilization; for a full month Rangneng did not leave the palace.

sentences.zh: 時宰相崔昭緯陰結茂貞及王行瑜，讓能所言悉漏之，茂貞乃以健兒數百雜市人，候昭緯與鄭延昌歸第，擁肩輿噪曰：「鳳翔無罪，幸公不加討以震驚都輦！

translations.literal: At that time the chief minister Cui Zhaowei was secretly allied with Maozhen and Wang Xingyu, and everything Rangneng said was leaked to them. Maozhen then sent several hundred stalwart soldiers mixed among the townspeople to wait until Zhaowei and Zheng Yanchang were returning to their residences; they surrounded the sedan chair and shouted: "Fengxiang is innocent—may you, sir, not launch a punitive campaign and alarm the capital!"
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister Cui Zhaowei was at that time secretly in league with Maozhen and Wang Xingyu, and Rangneng's every word was leaked to them. Maozhen then sent several hundred tough soldiers disguised among the townspeople to intercept Zhaowei and Zheng Yanchang on their way home. Surrounding their sedan chairs, they shouted, "Fengxiang is innocent—we beg you, sir, not to launch a punitive expedition and throw the capital into alarm!"

sentences.zh: 」昭緯曰：「上委杜太尉，吾等何知？

translations.literal: Zhaowei said: "The emperor has entrusted the matter to Grand Commandant Du—what do we know of it?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhaowei said, "The emperor has entrusted this to Grand Commandant Du—what do we know about it?"

sentences.zh: 」市人不識孰為太尉，即投瓦石妄擊，昭緯等走而免，遂喪其印。

translations.literal: The townspeople did not know which man was the Grand Commandant and so hurled tiles and stones at random; Zhaowei and the others fled and escaped, but lost their seals.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd did not know which man was the Grand Commandant and began hurling tiles and stones indiscriminately. Zhaowei and the others fled for their lives and escaped, but lost their official seals.

sentences.zh: 帝愈怒，捕首惡誅之。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier, seized the ringleaders, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's fury only increased; the ringleaders were arrested and put to death.

sentences.zh: 京師爭避亂，逃山谷間。

translations.literal: People in the capital scrambled to flee the turmoil and hid in the mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the capital people scrambled to escape the chaos, fleeing into the hills and ravines.

sentences.zh: 讓能諫帝曰：「茂貞固宜誅，然大盜適去，鳳翔國西門，又陛下新即位，願少寬假，以貞元故事姑息之，不可使怨望。

translations.literal: Rangneng remonstrated with the emperor, saying: "Maozhen indeed deserves execution, but the great bandits have only just departed, and Fengxiang is the western gate of the realm. Moreover, Your Majesty has only recently acceded; I beg you to show a little forbearance and, following the Zhenyuan precedent, treat him indulgently—you must not let him harbor resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Rangneng remonstrated with the emperor, saying, "Maozhen certainly deserves punishment, but the great rebels have only just been driven off, and Fengxiang is the empire's western gate. Your Majesty has moreover only lately taken the throne; I beg you to show a little restraint and, following the Zhenyuan precedent, treat Maozhen with forbearance rather than feed his resentment."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「今詔令不出城門，國制橈弱，賈生慟哭時也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Today edicts cannot even leave the city gates; the state's institutions are bent and weak—this is the time for Jia Yi's tears of grief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Today our edicts cannot even pass beyond the city gates; the state's institutions are crippled and weak. This is the hour of Jia Yi's lament.

sentences.zh: 朕顧奄奄度日，坐觀此邪！

translations.literal: Must I drag out my days and sit by watching this!
translations.idiomatic: Am I to drag out my days and sit idle while this goes on!

sentences.zh: 卿為我圖之，朕自以兵屬諸王。

translations.literal: You must devise a plan for me; I myself will place the troops under the princes."
translations.idiomatic: Devise a plan for me; I myself will commit the army to the princes."

sentences.zh: 」讓能曰：「陛下欲削滌僭嫚，剛主威，隆王室，此中外大臣所宜共成之，不宜專任臣。

translations.literal: Rangneng said: "Your Majesty wishes to cut down presumption and arrogance, stiffen imperial authority, and exalt the royal house—this is what ministers within and without ought to accomplish together; it should not be entrusted to your subject alone."
translations.idiomatic: Rangneng said, "Your Majesty wishes to purge insolence and overreach, restore imperial authority, and elevate the royal house. That is a task for all the great ministers together—it should not fall on me alone."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿，元輔，休戚與我均，何所避？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You are the chief minister; fortune and misfortune are shared with me—what is there to avoid?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are the chief minister; your fortunes are bound to mine—what is there to shrink from?"

sentences.zh: 」泣曰：「臣位宰相，所以未乞骸骨者，思有以報陛下，敢計身乎！

translations.literal: Weeping, he said: "Your subject holds the post of chief minister; the reason he has not yet begged to retire is that he thinks to repay Your Majesty—how would he dare count the cost to himself!
translations.idiomatic: Rangneng wept and said, "I remain in the post of chief minister only because I hope to repay Your Majesty—how could I count the cost to myself!

sentences.zh: 且陛下之心，憲祖心也，但時有所未便。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty's heart is the heart of Emperor Xianzong; only the times do not yet permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's heart is the heart of Emperor Xianzong; only the times are not yet ripe.

sentences.zh: 它日臣蒙晁錯之誅，顧不足弭七國患，然敢不奉詔！」

translations.literal: Another day your subject may suffer execution like Chao Cuo, which would hardly suffice to quell the disaster of the Seven Kingdoms—yet how would he dare not obey the edict!"
translations.idiomatic: One day I may suffer the fate of Chao Cuo, and even that would scarcely still the disaster of the Seven Kingdoms—yet how could I refuse your command?"

sentences.zh: 景福二年，以嗣覃王為招討使，神策將李钅歲副之，率師三萬送彥若趙鎮。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Jingfu era, the Succession Prince of Tan was made punitive commissioner, with Shence General Li Huai as his deputy; they led thirty thousand troops to escort Xu Yanruo to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingfu the Succession Prince of Tan was appointed punitive commissioner, with Shence General Li Huai as his deputy, and they led thirty thousand men to escort Xu Yanruo to his command.

sentences.zh: 昭緯內畏有功，密語茂貞曰：「上不喜兵，一出太尉。

translations.literal: Zhaowei inwardly feared those with merit and secretly told Maozhen: "The emperor dislikes warfare—as soon as the army moves, the Grand Commandant will be removed."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaowei, inwardly fearful of men with military credit, secretly told Maozhen, "The emperor dislikes war—as soon as the army marches, the Grand Commandant will be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 」茂貞乃悉兵迎戰盩厔，覃王敗，乘勝至三橋。

translations.literal: Maozhen then sent out his full force to meet the army at Zhouzhi; the Prince of Tan was defeated, and Maozhen pressed his victory as far as Sanqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen then marched out his entire force to give battle at Zhouzhi. The Prince of Tan was defeated, and Maozhen drove his victory as far as Sanqiao.

sentences.zh: 讓能曰：「臣固豫言之，臣請歸死以紓難。

translations.literal: Rangneng said: "Your subject forewarned of this beforehand; your subject asks to return and die to relieve the crisis."
translations.idiomatic: Rangneng said, "I warned of this in advance. Let me go back and accept death to ease the crisis."

sentences.zh: 」帝涕下不能已，曰：「與卿決矣！

translations.literal: The emperor wept without cease and said: "I have decided with you!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept without stopping and said, "My mind is made up with you."

sentences.zh: 」再貶雷州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Rangneng was again demoted to Registrar of Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rangneng was again demoted, this time to registrar of Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 茂貞尚駐兵請必殺之，乃賜死，年五十三。

translations.literal: Maozhen still kept his troops stationed and insisted that Rangneng must be killed; the emperor then ordered him to take poison. He was fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen kept his army encamped and demanded that Rangneng be put to death; the emperor then ordered him to commit suicide. He was fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 弟彥林，官御史中丞；

translations.literal: His younger brother Yanlin held the office of Censor-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yanlin served as Censor-in-Chief;

sentences.zh: 弘徽，戶部侍郎，皆及誅。

translations.literal: Honghui was Vice Minister of Revenue—both were executed along with him.
translations.idiomatic: and Honghui was Vice Minister of Revenue; both were executed with him.

sentences.zh: 帝痛之，後贈太師。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved for them and later posthumously made Rangneng Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned them deeply and later posthumously honored Rangneng as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子光乂，次子曉，不復仕。

translations.literal: His sons were Guangyi and, second, Xiao, who no longer entered office.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Guangyi and, second, Xiao, who never again entered government service.

sentences.zh: 曉入梁，貴顯於世。

translations.literal: Xiao entered Liang and rose to wealth and eminence in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao entered the service of Liang and rose to wealth and high standing.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：太宗以上聖之才，取孤隋，攘群盜，天下已平，用玄齡、如晦輔政。

translations.literal: The encomium says: With his supreme sage talent, Emperor Taizong took the isolated Sui, swept away the bandit hosts, and once the realm was pacified employed Xuanling and Ruhui to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Emperor Taizong, possessed of the highest sage talent, overthrew the tottering Sui, swept away the bandit armies, and once the realm was at peace put Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui at the head of his government.

sentences.zh: 興大亂之余，紀綱雕弛，而能興僕植僵，使號令典刑粲然罔不完，雖數百年猶蒙其功，可謂名宰相。

translations.literal: In the aftermath of great chaos, when institutions were broken and slack, they were able to raise the fallen and set the withered upright, so that commands and punishments stood brilliantly complete in every respect; even after several centuries men still benefited from their work—they may be called famous chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the wreckage of great upheaval, when law and order lay in ruins, they raised the fallen and restored the withered until commands and punishments shone forth complete in every detail; centuries later the realm still reaped their benefit—they were truly great chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 然求所以致之之跡，逮不可見，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet when one seeks the traces of how this was achieved, they cannot even be seen—why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Yet when one tries to trace how they accomplished it, the trail vanishes altogether—why should that be?

sentences.zh: 唐柳芳有言：「帝定禍亂，而房、杜不言功；

translations.literal: Tang's Liu Fang once said: "When the emperor settled chaos and disaster, Fang and Du did not speak of their merit;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang of Tang once observed, "When the emperor quelled chaos and disaster, Fang and Du did not speak of their own merit;

sentences.zh: 王、魏善諫，而房、杜讓其直；

translations.literal: Wang and Wei were skilled at remonstrance, yet Fang and Du yielded to them the straight word;
translations.idiomatic: Wang and Wei were skilled at remonstrance, yet Fang and Du yielded them the frank word;

sentences.zh: 英、衛善兵，而房、杜濟以文。

translations.literal: Ying and Wei were skilled at warfare, yet Fang and Du complemented them with civil culture.
translations.idiomatic: the Ying and Wei dukes were skilled at warfare, yet Fang and Du complemented them with civil culture.

sentences.zh: 持眾美效之君。

translations.literal: They held up every excellence before the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: They held every excellence up before the ruler.

sentences.zh: 是後，新進更用事，玄齡身處要地，不吝權，善始以終，此其成令名者。

translations.literal: Afterward, newer men wielded power in turn; Xuanling stood in a key position yet did not begrudge authority, and from beginning to end did well—this is how he won a lasting name.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, as newer men rose to power in turn, Xuanling occupied the highest place yet did not hoard authority, and from first to last conducted himself with integrity—this is how he earned a lasting reputation.

sentences.zh: 」諒其然乎！

translations.literal: Can one doubt that this is so!
translations.idiomatic: Who can doubt that this is so!

sentences.zh: 如晦雖任事日淺，觀玄齡許與及帝所親款，則謨謀果有大過人者。

translations.literal: Although Ruhui's tenure was brief, judging from Xuanling's praise of him and the emperor's intimate regard, his counsel and resolution were indeed far above other men.
translations.idiomatic: Though Ruhui served only briefly, judging from Xuanling's esteem for him and the emperor's intimate regard, his counsel and decisiveness were truly far above ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 方君臣明良，志葉議從，相資以成，固千載之遇，蕭、曹之勳，不足進焉。

translations.literal: When ruler and minister were enlightened and good, wills joined and plans accorded, and they supported one another to completion—it was indeed a meeting of a thousand years; the achievements of Xiao and Cao are not worth mentioning beside them.
translations.idiomatic: When ruler and minister are enlightened and in harmony, wills aligned and counsel agreed, and they strengthen one another to completion—that is a rendezvous of a millennium; the achievements of Xiao He and Cao Can scarcely bear comparison.

sentences.zh: 雖然，宰相所以代天者也，輔贊彌縫而藏諸用，使斯人由而不知，非明哲曷臻是哉？

translations.literal: Even so, the chief minister stands in for Heaven: he assists, harmonizes, mends, and conceals his work in practice, so that men pass through it without knowing—without wisdom and clarity, how could one reach this?
translations.idiomatic: Even so, the chief minister stands in Heaven's place: he assists, harmonizes, and mends, hiding his work in the very fabric of government so that men benefit without knowing how—without wisdom and clarity, how could anyone attain this?

sentences.zh: 彼揚己取名，了然使戶曉者，蓋房、杜之細邪！

translations.literal: Those who display themselves to win fame and make their deeds plain to every household—are they not precisely what Fang and Du disdained!
translations.idiomatic: As for those who parade themselves to win fame and make their deeds plain to every household—that is precisely what Fang and Du held in contempt!
